BURHAN:v4p174/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p174/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p174/r1.claim: Sawāʾ can mean the middle, hence an even, just, or true word in the call to a common position.

BURHAN:v4p174/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p174/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الربيع
BURHAN:v4p174/r2.claim: Ibn Abī al-Rabīʿ says sawāʾ raises an overt noun only when that noun is coordinated with the pronoun governed by sawāʾ; this is permitted for a conjunct though not its counterpart.
BURHAN:v4p174/r2.anchor: قال ابن أبي الربيع وسواء لا يرفع الظاهر إلا إذا كان معطوفا على المضمر في سواء

ITQAN:v2p356/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p356/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p356/r6.claim: سواء means justice or equality; an anonymous poem uses it in a comparison of outcomes.
ITQAN:v2p356/r6.anchor: قال عدل قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول الشاعر

TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r3.claim: The call to worship God alone also rejects humans taking one another as lords; the verse closes by calling for submission to God.
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r3.anchor: أن لا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r1.claim: Because the Prophet longed for their faith, God directs him from disputation to an impartial, fair invitation that sound reason can accept.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r1.anchor: كان عليه السلام حريصا على إيمانهم فأمره الله تعالى بأن يعدل عن طريق المجادلة

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r2.claim: Taʿālaw means attend to the proposed matter and examine it, not physically move; the word began with rising from a low place to a high one.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r2.anchor: والمراد تعيين ما دعوا إليه والتوجه إلى النظر فيه وإن لم يكن انتقالا من مكان

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r3.claim: The shared word is one on which messengers and scriptures agree, with fairness between the parties and no bias toward either.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r3.anchor: لا يختلف فيها الرسل والكتب فيها إنصاف من بعضنا لبعض ولا ميل فيها لأحد

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r4.claim: Worshipping Allah alone means affirming his oneness in worship and devoting worship sincerely to him.

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r5.claim: Shirk means granting another a share in the right to worship or considering another worthy of worship.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r5.anchor: ولا نجعل غيره شريكا في استحقاق العبادة ولا نراه أهلا لأن نعبده

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r6.claim: Taking one another as lords includes calling Ezra or Christ God’s son and obeying rabbis’ invented permissions and prohibitions, although they are fellow humans.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r6.anchor: بأن نقول عزير ابن الله والمسيح ابن الله ولا نطيع الأحبار فيما أحدثوا

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r7.speaker: الفضيل
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r7.claim: Al-Fudayl says he does not care whether someone obeys a creature while disobeying the Creator or prays away from the qibla.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r7.anchor: وعن الفضيل لا أبالي أطعت مخلوقا في معصية الخالق أم صليت لغير القبلة

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r8.claim: If they refuse tawhid and reject associating partners with God, tell them the proof has been established and acknowledge that the Muslims have submitted.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r8.anchor: لزمتكم الحجة فاعترفوا بأنا مسلمون دونكم

BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r9.claim: The Prophet’s letter to Caesar invites him to Islam, promising safety from worldly captivity and the afterlife’s punishment, doubled reward, and responsibility for the Arisiyyin if he refuses.
BURSEVI:v2p37#2/r9.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب إلى قيصر

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r1.claim: Heraclius recognized the Prophet’s signs from the old scriptures and said he would kiss his feet if he met him, but feared losing his kingship.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r1.anchor: وعرفها ممن جاء بكتابه فقال : لو كنت عنده لقبلت قدميه

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r2.speaker: هرقل
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r2.claim: Heraclius wrote that he acknowledged Muhammad as a prophet but could not leave the old religion God had chosen for Jesus.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r2.anchor: إنا نشهد أنك نبي ولكنا لا نستطيع أن نترك الدين القديم

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r3.claim: The Prophet said Heraclius’s kingdom would endure until the Day of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r3.anchor: فعجب النبي عليه السلام فقال : "لقد ثبت ملكهم إلى يوم القيامة أبدا"

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r4.claim: Khosrow tore up the Prophet’s letter and the envoy returned after Khosrow tried to kill him; the Prophet prayed that their rule be torn apart, and it was.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r4.anchor: فدعا عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : "خرق الله ملكهم فلا ملك لهم أبدا"

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r5.claim: The inward lesson is that every religion rests on sincere servitude: as one worships only Allah, one seeks no other besides him.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r5.anchor: أصول الأديان كلها إخلاص العبودية كما قال تعالى :

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r6.claim: The inward prohibition against making people lords rejects seeking provision through them and seeing worldly events as mediated by them.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r6.anchor: في طلب الرزق ورؤية الأمور من الوسائط {فإن تولوا}

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r7.claim: Those who turn away are to be told that Muslims surrender to God in tawhid, sincere worship, and the denial of shirk.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r7.anchor: مستسلمون لما دعانا الله إليه من التوحيد والإخلاص في العبودية ونفى الشرك

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r8.claim: The demand for testimony is so disbelievers will testify to Muslims’ monotheism at the Resurrection, making their testimony evidence against themselves.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r8.anchor: والسر في الإشهاد على الإسلام ليشهد الكفار لهم يوم القيامة على الإسلام والتوحيد

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r9.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r9.claim: The Prophet told Abu Saʿid that every jinn, human, or other being within an adhan’s range will testify for the caller on the Day of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r9.anchor: كما قال النبي عليه السلام لأبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه : "إني أراك تحب الغنم

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r10.claim: Tawhid is the firmest handhold and root of all roots; sincere adherence receives acceptance from the unseen.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r10.anchor: فالتوحيد هي العروة الوثقى وأصل الأصول يهب من جانب الغيب لمن أخلصه قبول القبول

BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r11.claim: One should study the Quran’s meanings instead of turning away, pursue knowledge and deeds, and avoid ignorance and error before death.
BURSEVI:v2p37#3/r11.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا يخالف كتاب الله بالإعراض عن فحاويه وعدم التدبر في معانيه

ELMALILI:3:64/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r1.claim: The verse shows how diverse peoples, religions, scriptures, and consciences can unite around a foundational truth; Islam offers universal, clear, straight guidance and a law of freedom beyond Arabs and Persians.

ELMALILI:3:64/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r2.claim: The shared call to worship God alone without partners or human lords is the broadest and most authoritative common conscience; religious progress lies in universality, not sectarian particularity.
ELMALILI:3:64/r2.anchor: Terakkiyât-ı dîniye vicdanların iftirak ifade eden hususiyetlerinde değil, külliyetinde ve genişliğindedir.

ELMALILI:3:64/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r3.claim: This shared confession is the basis of freedom and equality: people must not treat one another as absolute lords, masters, or judges, but measure conduct by God's command and pleasure.
ELMALILI:3:64/r3.anchor: İşte hürriyet ve müsâvat davasının bütün miftâh-ı halli buradadır. Birbirimizi rab, mevlâ, hâkim-i mutlak tanımayalım

ELMALILI:3:64/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r4.claim: There should be no pledge of obedience to anyone besides God against the right; all are God's servants and accountable to Him, and mutual allegiance is valid only from this standpoint.
ELMALILI:3:64/r4.anchor: Allah’ı bırakıp da O’nun mâdûnunda ve hakkın hilâfında bir tâbi‘iyet mîsâkımız olmasın, hepimiz Allah’a kul olalım

ELMALILI:3:64/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r5.claim: People must respect one another's rights and obey God-given duties for God's sake; disputes should be settled by right and law rather than anyone's personal desire.
ELMALILI:3:64/r5.anchor: her ihtilâf mülâhaza-i hak ve kānûn-ı hak ile hallolunur. Ve hiçbir kimsenin arzû-yı mücerredi hâkim olmaz.

ELMALILI:3:64/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r6.claim: Therefore Jesus should be regarded as God's servant and messenger, not as Lord; popes, kings, and leaders are likewise assessed by obedience to God and pursuit of truth.
ELMALILI:3:64/r6.anchor: Îsâ’yı da rab tanımayalım. Onu da Allah’ın bir kulu ve bir resûlü tanıyalım. Kezâlik papalar, krallar, rüesâ hep böyle

ELMALILI:3:64/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r7.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:3:64/r7.claim: In response to a question, the Prophet told believing People of the Book that obeying popes and others merely because of their own words amounted to taking them as lords.
ELMALILI:3:64/r7.anchor: Vâki‘olan bir suale karşı Resûlullah ehl-i kitabdan iman edenlere

ELMALILI:3:64/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r8.claim: The immediate context especially addresses Christians who make Jesus Lord; translating the expression as teacher does not resolve the issue while the doctrine of Trinity remains, since God is still the true teacher in 3:48.
ELMALILI:3:64/r8.anchor: Bugün bazı İncil tercemelerinde bunun muallim demek olduğu gösterilmiş ise de akīde-i teslis mevcud iken bu tevil kâfi olamaz.

ELMALILI:3:64/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:64/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:64/r9.claim: The People of the Book preferred division over true monotheistic unity, each claiming Abraham as their own by calling him Jewish or Christian.
ELMALILI:3:64/r9.anchor: her biri kendilerine nisbet ederek “Yahudî idi” veya “Nasrânî idi” dediler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r1.claim: After the preceding clarification of Jesus’ status and the invitation to mutual imprecation, the passage turns from debate to its main purpose.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r1.anchor: “mübâhele”ye davet ile son verildikten sonra burada asıl amaca geçilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r2.claim: The earlier explanations aim to remove barriers to dialogue and find common ground, rather than deepen conflict or stage sterile disputation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r2.anchor: taraflar arasında çekişmenin derinleştirilmesi ve kuru bir münazara yapılması gibi bir amaç taşımamakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r3.claim: One interpretation takes “People of the Book” here to mean the Christians of Najran.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r3.anchor: a) Necran hıristiyanlarının, b) Medine yahudilerinin, c) hem yahudi hem hıristiyanların birlikte kastedildiğine dair görüşler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r4.claim: A second interpretation takes “People of the Book” here to mean the Jews of Medina.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r4.anchor: a) Necran hıristiyanlarının, b) Medine yahudilerinin, c) hem yahudi hem hıristiyanların birlikte kastedildiğine dair görüşler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r5.claim: A third interpretation takes “People of the Book” to include Jews and Christians together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r5.anchor: a) Necran hıristiyanlarının, b) Medine yahudilerinin, c) hem yahudi hem hıristiyanların birlikte kastedildiğine dair görüşler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r6.claim: Despite exegetes who narrow the audience by occasion of revelation, the letter to Heraclius indicates a general call to adherents of religions grounded in original monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r6.anchor: bu âyette aslî şekliyle tevhid inancına dayalı din mensuplarına genel bir çağrının bulunduğu anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r7.claim: Sound dialogue requires mutual respect and avoiding subjective language and attitudes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r7.anchor: karşılıklı saygı esasına riayet edilmesi, sübjektif üslûp ve tavırlardan kaçınılması gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r8.claim: The verse models a gracious opening that treats its audience as people entrusted with scripture and gives them due regard.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r8.anchor: muhatapları Allah’ın kitabına ehil sayan gönül alıcı ve nazik bir hitapla söze başlanarak onlara değer verilmesi gerektiğine işaret etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r9.claim: The Qur’an directs Muslims to use the best manner when discussing with the People of the Book and opposing their mistaken conduct.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r10.claim: Some People of the Book possess faith that the Qur’an approves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r10.anchor: Kur’an’ın tasvip ettiği imana sahip insanlar bulunduğuna dikkat çekilmiştir (Âl-i İmrân 3/110, 113, 199)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r11.claim: The Qur’an says Muslims rejoice when Christians defeat the fire-worshippers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r11.anchor: hıristiyanların ateşperestlere karşı zafer kazanacakları haber verildikten sonra müslümanların bundan sevinç duyacakları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r12.claim: Condemnations of the People of the Book clarify ideas and prompt self-examination rather than express subjective hostility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r12.anchor: bunların sübjektif bir tavrı yansıtmadığı, bilâkis fikirlerin billûrlaştırılmasına ve muhatabın kendi kendini sorgulamasını sağlamaya yönelik olduğu görülmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r14.claim: The phrase rendered “a common word” is glossed as just, upright, moderate, fair, and equitable speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r14.anchor: “âdilâne, dosdoğru, orta yolun ifadesi olan bir söz, adalet ve insaf ölçülerine uygun bir söz” şeklinde açıklanmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r15.claim: “Between us and you” refers to shared principles between Muslims and adherents of religions whose original identity upheld belief in one God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r15.anchor: burada müslümanlar ile aslî hüviyeti itibariyle tek Tanrı inancının savunucusu olan din mensupları arasındaki ortak ilkelerin özünün kastedildiği açıkça anlaşılır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r16.claim: The foundational shared principle is worshipping Allah alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r16.anchor: Âyette bu ilkelerin en temel noktası “yalnız Allah’a kulluk etme” şeklinde belirtilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r17.claim: Worship of Allah alone requires both rejecting all partners with Him and refusing to take any other authority, person, or power as lord.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r17.anchor: a) Hiçbir şeyi Allah’a ortak saymamak, b) Allah’ın dışında hiçbir merci, kişi veya gücü rab kabul etmemek.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r18.claim: The call recalls the prophets’ common message and warns that violating either condition compromises pure monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r18.anchor: Ehl-i kitap, peygamberlerin tebliğ faaliyetinin ortak çizgisine çağrılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r19.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r19.claim: Elmalılı says Islam shows how diverse consciences, nations, religions, and scriptures can unite around a fundamental true word, a universal guidance not confined to one people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r19.anchor: Burada muhtelif vicdanların, milletlerin, dinlerin, kitapların temel bir vicdanda, bir hak sözde nasıl birleştirilebilecekleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r20.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r20.claim: He argues that no broader, more commanding conscience can be found than unity in worshipping Allah alone without associating partners or making one another lords.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r20.anchor: Vicdan birliğinden daha geniş, daha hâkim hiçbir vicdan bulmak mümkün değildir ki onun arkasına düşülsün.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r21.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r21.claim: Religious progress lies in the breadth and comprehensiveness of conscience, not in traits that separate communities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r21.anchor: Din alanındaki ilerleme ve gelişmeler, vicdanların birbirinden ayrı düşen özelliklerinde değil, bütüncüllüğünde ve genişliğindedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r22.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r22.claim: Freedom and equality rest on refusing to make one another lords and gathering under the claim that only Allah is lord.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r22.anchor: Bütün özgürlük ve eşitlik çağrılarının temeli şu “bir sözde, bir vicdanda toplanır: Allah’ı bırakıp da içimizden bazıları diğer bazılarını rab edinmesin.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r23.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r23.claim: People should obey others only in obedience to Allah’s command and should not violate one another’s rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r23.anchor: birbirimizin hakkına tecavüz etmeyelim, başkalarına ancak Allah’ın buyruğuna itaat kastıyla itaat edelim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r24.claim: The verse emphasizes both unity of divinity and unity of lordship: belief and attachment to one being alone as God and Lord.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r24.anchor: hem “ulûhiyyet birliği” hem de “rubûbiyyet birliği”, yani tanrı ve rab olarak tek bir varlığa inanıp bağlanmanın kaçınılmazlığı üzerinde durulmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r25.claim: Unity of divinity means worshipping Allah as the sole power of the transcendent realm.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r25.anchor: birincisi Allah’a fizik ötesi âlemle ilgili yegâne gücün kendisine ait olduğu inancıyla tapmayı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r26.claim: Unity of lordship means making Allah’s will govern life and worshipping only as He wills.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r26.anchor: ikincisi de hayata sadece Allah’ın iradesini hâkim kılmayı, yalnız O’nun istediği biçimde kulluk etmeyi ifade eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r27.claim: Judaism and Christianity share Islam’s affirmation that Allah alone is worthy of worship, but later beliefs and practices undermined divine oneness and exclusive worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r27.anchor: zamanla bu dinlerin mesuplarınca benimsenen bazı inanç ve davranışlar, Tanrı’nın tek olduğu ve Allah’tan başka hiçbir varlığın rab sayılamayacağı telakkisini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r28.claim: Despite prophetic warnings against shirk, Jews called Uzayr and Christians Jesus the son of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r28.anchor: yahudiler Üzeyir’i, hıristiyanlar da Îsâ aleyhisselâmı Allah’ın oğlu olarak nitelendirmişler (bk. Tevbe 9/30)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r29.claim: Christians said Allah is one of three; Jews nationalized God and obscured His status as creator and Lord of all the universe.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r30.claim: Even the present, altered Torah and Gospels affirm that God is one and that Jesus was sent to the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r30.anchor: tahrif edilmiş şekliyle bile bugün mevcut Tevrat ve İnciller’deki ifadeler Tanrı’nın “bir” olduğunu ve Hz. Îsâ’nın İsrâiloğulları’na “gönderildiği”ni belirtmektedir:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r31.claim: Since Allah owns and sustains every creature and gives it its form, worship requires heartfelt submission to His will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r31.anchor: evrendeki bütün varlıkların sahibi ve onları terbiye eden, onlara dilediği kıvamı veren yüce Allah olduğuna göre (Fâtiha 1/3)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r32.claim: Christians elevated Jesus, while Jews and Christians gave clergy godlike authority, departing from servitude to Allah alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r32.anchor: din adamlarına (ahbâr ve ruhbân) Tanrı benzeri bir otorite tanıyarak yalnız Allah’a kul olma çizgisinin dışına çıkmışlardı (bk. Tevbe 9/31).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r33.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r33.claim: In the report from Adî b. Hâtim, taking religious leaders as lords means accepting their declarations of what is lawful or forbidden and following them, even without worshipping them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r33.anchor: Adî b. Hâtim ile Hz. Peygamber arasında geçen şu konuşma, burada yer alan “Allah’ı bırakıp da içimizden bazıları diğer bazılarını rab edinmesin” ifadesinin anlaşılmasını kolaylaştırmaktadır:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r34.claim: Modern Western safeguards and intellectual criticism of religion as a tool of domination can be positive responses to the Qur’anic call.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r34.anchor: Kur’an’ın bu konudaki çağrısına uyma açısından olumlu bir gelişme sayılabilirse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r35.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r35.claim: Those measures remain limited to preventing the use of religion as an instrument of domination and exploitation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r35.anchor: bu tedbirlerin dinin egemenlik ve sömürü aracı olarak kullanılmasını engelleme hedefiyle sınırlı kaldığı inkâr edilemez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r36.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r36.claim: Clergy are still regarded as authorities who can decide how to worship God and, among Christians, grant forgiveness in God’s name.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r36.anchor: din adamları, mürşid, yol gösteren, uyaran kişiler olmanın ötesinde tanrıya nasıl kulluk edileceğine karar verebilen ve hıristiyanlarca tanrı adına affedebilen merciler olarak görülmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r37.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r37.claim: Christians also regard Jesus as a superhuman protector and guardian.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r37.anchor: hıristiyanlar tarafından Hz. Îsâ koruyan, gözeten insan üstü bir varlık olarak telakki edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r38.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r38.claim: For these reasons, the People of the Book still need to consider the call carefully on matters of belief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r38.anchor: inanç esasları bakımından Ehl-i kitabın bu çağrı üzerinde dikkatle durması ihtiyacının devam ettiği kuşkusuzdur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r39.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r39.claim: A separate harmful outcome arises when reactions to religious domination turn into hostility toward religion and belief themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r39.anchor: tepkilerin “din”e ve “inanma”ya karşı bir tavır haline dönüşen biçimlerini de kaş yaparken göz çıkarmaya varan ayrı bir olumsuz sonuç olarak hatırlamak gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r40.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r40.claim: Kurtubî reads the verse as disallowing personal inclination and arbitrary judgment in deriving religious rulings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r40.anchor: İslâm’da dinî hükümlerin çıkarılmasında kişisel eğilimlerin ve keyfî takdirlerin hâkim kılınmasına müsaade edilmediği anlamı üzerinde durur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r41.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r41.claim: He says the verse indicates that istihsan unsupported by a legal proof is invalid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r41.anchor: şer‘î delile dayandırılmayan “istihsan”ın geçersiz olduğuna delâlet bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r42.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r42.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r42.claim: He also says the verse rejects the Rafidites’ claim that an imam’s word binds without showing its basis in the Sharia.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r42.anchor: şer‘î dayanağını göstermeden imamın sözünün bağlayıcılığını iddia eden Râfizîler’in bu yaklaşımının reddedildiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r43.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r43.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r43.claim: The criticism is directed at arbitrary inference that lacks a valid basis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r43.anchor: burada geçerli bir dayanaktan yoksun keyfî istidlâllere yöneltilmiş bir eleştiri söz konusudur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r44.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r44.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r44.claim: Properly grounded istihsan, setting aside the usual rule for stronger evidence or principles such as benefit, fairness, and honesty, is accepted and practiced by nearly all Muslim scholars despite disputes over terminology.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:64/r44.anchor: istihsan delili –isimlendirme ihtilâfları bir yana– içerik olarak hemen bütün İslâm âlimlerince kabul edilmiş ve uygulanmıştır

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r12.speaker: الحسن والسدي ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r12.claim: Hasan, al-Suddi, and Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr say the verse was revealed concerning the delegation from Najran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r12.anchor: نزلت في وفد نجران، قاله الحسن، والسدي، ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd says that after the people of Najran refused the invitation to mutual imprecation, they were invited to the easier common word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p192/r13.anchor: قال ابن زيد: لما أبى أهل نجران ما دعوا إليه من الملاعنة، دعوا إلى أيسر من ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about priests and monks and was sent by the Prophet to Jaʿfar and his companions in Abyssinia, where Jaʿfar recited it before the Negus and Abyssinian leaders.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في القسيسين والرهبان، بعث بها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى جعفر وأصحابه بالحبشة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r2.speaker: قتادة والربيع وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r2.claim: They say it concerned the Jews of Medina who disputed about Abraham.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة، والربيع، وابن جريج: في يهود المدينة، وهم الذين حاجوا في إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r3.claim: Another reported occasion says Jews and Christians asked Muhammad whether he only wanted them to say of him what the Jews said of Ezra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r3.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى، قالوا: يا محمد! ما تريد إلا أن نقول فيك ما قالت اليهود في عزير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r4.claim: The address to the People of the Book can include everyone given scripture, and the Messenger used it for Jews; in this context Christians are the likelier referent because the argument and proposed imprecation concerned them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r4.anchor: ولفظ: يا أهل الكتاب، يعم كل من أوتي كتابا، ولذلك دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اليهود بالآية، والأقرب حمله على النصارى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r5.claim: Calling them People of the Book taunts them into listening and reminds them that recipients of God's scripture ought to follow it; after proofs failed and they refused imprecation, the Prophet shifted to a conciliatory invitation to an equitable common word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r5.anchor: هزا لهم في استماع ما يلقى إليهم، وتنبيها على أن من كان أهل كتاب من الله ينبغي أن يتبع كتاب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r6.speaker: أبو السمال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r6.claim: Abū al-Sammāl has two variant vocalizations of كلمة, likened respectively to ضربة and سدرة; the discussion had appeared at 3:39.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال: كلمة، كضربة، و: كلمة، كسدرة، وتقدم هذا عند قوله: مصدقا بكلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses the word as the declaration “There is no god but God.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا إله إلا الله، وهذا تفسير المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the singular كلمة for a plural saying because Arabic can use a singular for speech or words; the cited verse of poetry supports singular wording for a collective expression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r8.anchor: وعبر بالكلمة عن الكلمات، لأن الكلمة قد تطلقها العرب على الكلام، وإلى هذا ذهب الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r9.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows the linked words to count as one word because omitting any component breaks the whole; the tawḥīd formula confines divinity to God only when its parts are combined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r9.anchor: لكون الكلمات مرتبطة بعضها ببعض، فصارت في قوة الكلمة الواحدة إذا اختل جزء منها اختلت الكلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r10.claim: Most readers make سواء genitive as an adjective; al-Ḥasan reads it accusative, parsed by al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī as a verbal noun or possibly a circumstantial accusative, while the common sense is “equal.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سواء، بالجر على الصفة. وقرأ الحسن: سواء، بالنصب، وخرجه الحوفي والزمخشري على أنه مصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r1.claim: The verse invites them to a fair, equitable word between the two groups.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r1.anchor: والمعنى: إلى كلمة عادلة بيننا وبينكم. وقال أبو عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites an Arabic idiom meaning that when someone invites you to an equitable course, you should accept.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: تقول العرب: قد دعاك فلان إلى سواء فاقبل منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r3.claim: A reading in ʿAbd Allāh's codex has عدل in place of سواء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the word as a level, upright word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أي كلمة مستوية، أي مستقيمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r5.claim: Another gloss takes سواء to mean a direct or moderate course.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives سواء a contextual sense of equal standing: a shared truth in which young and old alike are equal, answering the audience's practice of making some people lords over others; people naturally welcome such equality. He distinguishes this from justice, which could describe coercively offering a captive conversion or death, and says the word still includes justice under every reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r6.anchor: وهو أنه دعاهم إلى معان جميع الناس فيها مستوون، صغيرهم وكبيرهم، وقد كانت سيرة المدعوين أن يتخذ بعضهم بعضا أربابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān dismisses Ibn ʿAṭiyya's extended discussion as verbose and without useful result.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r7.anchor: انتهى كلامه، وهو تكثير لا طائل تحته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r8.claim: The الظرف in the phrase is apparently governed by سواء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r9.claim: One parse makes ألا نعبد genitive as an appositive replacing كلمة; another makes it the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning “it is that we worship only God.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r9.anchor: ألا نعبد إلا الله موضع: أن، جر على البدل من: كلمة، بدل شيء من شيء، ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع خبر لمبتدأ محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r10.claim: A proposed parse ends the preceding clause at سواء and makes ألا نعبد a subject whose predicate is بيننا وبينكم, describing كلمة; Abū Ḥayyān rejects it because the sentence lacks a link to its antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r10.anchor: والجملة صفة للكلمة، وهذا وهم لعرو الجملة من رابط يربطها بالموصوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r11.claim: Making the clause nominative through the adverb works only under al-Akhfash's and Kufan grammarians' view that an adverb can govern without a licensing support, which Basran grammarians deny.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r11.anchor: ولا يصح إلا على مذهب الأخفش والكوفيين حيث أجازوا إعمال الظرف من غير اعتماد، والبصريون يمنعون ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r12.speaker: علي بن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r12.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā proposes an implied phrase “a word equal between us and you in which is refusal to worship another”; this makes ألا نعبد the subject of سواء, but requires a weakly omitted link فيها.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p194/r12.anchor: وجوز علي بن عيسى أن يكون التقدير: إلى كلمة مستو بيننا وبينكم فيها الامتناع من عبادة غير الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r1.claim: The invitation means that worship is reserved for God alone, with no partner attributed to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r1.anchor: والمعنى: أن نفرد الله وحده بالعبادة ولا نشرك به شيئا، أي: لا نجعل له شريكا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r2.claim: شيئا can be a direct object or a verbal noun meaning any act of association; because the verb is negated, the negation extends to all its complements, including object, action, time, place, and manner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r2.anchor: وشيئا يحتمل أن يكون مفعولا به، ويحتمل أن يكون مصدرا أي شيئا من الإشراك، والفعل في سياق النفي، فيعم متعلقاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r3.speaker: مقاتل والزجاج وعكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r3.claim: They explain taking one another as lords as believing in one another's divinity and worshipping them, as with Ezra and Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r3.anchor: فنعتقد فيهم الإلهية ونعبدهم على ذلك: كعزير وعيسى، قاله مقاتل، والزجاج، وعكرمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the phrase as people prostrating to one another or obeying bishops and leaders in unbelief and sin, treating their commands as religious law; the parallel is 9:31.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r4.anchor: أو لا نطيع الأساقفة والرؤساء فيما أمروا به من الكفر والمعاصي ونجعل طاعتهم شرعا. قاله ابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r5.claim: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim told the Prophet they had not worshipped their clerics; the Prophet asked whether the clerics had made things lawful and forbidden and they had followed, and ʿAdī agreed, to which the Prophet replied, “That was it.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195/r5.anchor: وعن عدي بن حاتم: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله. قال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.claim: The reciprocal “some of us, others” subtly denies divinity: people share human nature, so one like oneself cannot be God; claiming divinity for humans is even less plausible than objecting to following prophets who are human, as the cited verses show.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.anchor: وفي قوله: بعضنا بعضا، إشارة لطيفة، وهي أن البعضية تنافي الإلهية إذ هي تماثل في البشرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.claim: The three negative clauses overlap and reinforce God's exclusive worship, an emphatic expansion suited to people deeply attached to worshipping others; Christians combined all three by worshipping Jesus, calling God “third of three,” and making clerics lords through obedience and prostration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.anchor: والنصارى جمعوا بين الأفعال الثلاثة: عبدوا عيسى، وأشركوا بقولهم: ثالث ثلاثة، واتخذوا أحبارهم أربابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says taking people as lords means treating them as God's equals by accepting their rulings that forbid or permit what God did not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.anchor: قال الطبري: في قوله: أربابا من دون الله أنزلوهم منزلة ربهم في قبول التحريم والتحليل لما لم يحرمه الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says this supports rejecting free-standing legal preference without revealed evidence and the Rawāfiḍ claim that an imam's ruling must be accepted without proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على بطلان القول بالاستحسان المجرد الذي لا يستند إلى دليل شرعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.claim: If they turn away from the common word, Muslims should make them witness their own adherence to it; the wording sharply contrasts their refusal with Muslims' acceptance and obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.anchor: فإن تولوا عن الكلمة السواء فأشهدوهم أنكم منقادون إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.claim: Using “bear witness” for knowledge intensifies the point by presenting an inward understanding as though it were sensibly witnessed and present.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.anchor: وعبر عن العلم بالشهادة على سبيل المبالغة، إذ خرج ذلك من حيز المعقول إلى حيز المشهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the command publicly announces disagreement and confronts the rejecters as a reproach and threat, warning them to see the consequence of turning away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هذا أمر بإعلام بمخالفتهم ومواجهتهم بذلك، وإشهادهم على معنى التوبيخ والتهديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r3.claim: The passage uses warning and pointing, paired emphatic particles, separation, and focus in “knowing the corrupters” and “guardian of the believers”; it also uses singular for a plural in كلمة and a generic designation in أهل الكتاب when understood as Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r3.anchor: قيل: وجمعت هذه الآيات من البلاغة: التنبيه والإشارة والجمع بين حرفي التأكيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r4.claim: Other rhetorical devices include repeated إلا الله, إن الله, the People of the Book address, and Abraham; أربابا is a metaphor likening obedience in lawmaking to the rightful Lord, and أولى/ولي form paronomasia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r4.anchor: والتشبيه في: أربابا، لما أطاعوهم في التحليل والتحريم، وأذعنوا إليهم أطلق عليه: أربابا تشبيها بالرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r5.claim: The broad address “People of the Book” is an example of concise general address, comparable to Abraham's repeated “Father” and the cited poems.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p203/r5.anchor: والإجمال في الخطاب في: يا أهل الكتاب، تعالوا يا أهل الكتاب، لم تحاجون، كقول إبراهيم: يا أبت. يا أبت

QASHANI:3:64/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:64/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:64/r1.claim: The common word between the People of the Book and Muslims is divine unity, on which no prophet or scripture has ever differed.
QASHANI:3:64/r1.anchor: لم يختلف في كلمة التوحيد نبي ولا كتاب قط

QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r9.claim: The common word offered to the People of the Book is the oneness of God, witnessed as the sole originator of things.
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r9.anchor: هي كلمة التوحيد وإفراد الحق سبحانه في إنشاء الأشياء بالشهود

QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r10.claim: Worshipping God alone inwardly means not directing one's secret toward any creature; no other should be one's aim or object of witnessing, and the self is the first other to efface from awareness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r10.anchor: لا تطالع بسرك مخلوقا . وكما لا يكون غيره معبودك فينبغي ألا يكون غيره مقصودك ولا مشهودك

QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r11.claim: Not taking people as lords is shown by abandoning praise, blame, complaint, and doubt about them, and by attributing no particle of independent agency to them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r11.anchor: ويظهر صدق هذا بترك المدح والذم لهم . ونفي الشكوى والشك عنهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r12.speaker: لبيد
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r12.claim: Labid's verse is cited as the truest Arab saying: everything except God is false and every delight must pass away.
QUSHAYRI:v1p150/r12.anchor: قال ( أصدق كلمة قالتها العرب قول لبيد ) ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل . . . وكل نعيم لا محالة زائل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r1.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r1.anchor: نزلت في وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r2.anchor: نزلت في وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r3.anchor: وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى والحسن وابن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r4.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r4.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr is also cited for the view that the address concerns the Christian delegation from Najrān.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r4.anchor: الحسن وابن زيد ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r5.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn Jurayj report that it was revealed about the Jews of Medina.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r5.anchor: وروى عن قتادة والربيع وابن جريج أنها نزلت في يهود المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r6.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī says it concerns both groups of the People of the Book; a later verifier prefers this because the wording is general.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r6.anchor: وذهب أبو علي الجبائي أنها نزلت في الفريقين من أهل الكتاب واستظهره بعض المحققين لعمومه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes kalimah to mean speech; its use for a full utterance is a metonymic figure, though extending it to an incomplete compound has no attested precedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r8.anchor: أي كلام كما قال الزجاج واطلاقها على ذلك في كلامهم من باب المجاز المرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r9.claim: Another analysis treats kalimah as metaphor; al-Ālūsī considers that interpretation plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r9.anchor: وقيل : إنه من باب الاستعارة وليس بالبعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r10.claim: A lightened reading has kasra on kāf and a quiescent lām, with transfer of the vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r10.anchor: وقرئ ( كلمة ) بكسر الكاف وإسكان اللام على التخفيف والنقل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, and Qatāda explain sawāʾ as justice.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r11.anchor: أي عدل قاله ابن عباس والربيع وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r12.claim: Sawāʾ may mean equal: Torah, Gospel, and Qurʾān do not differ on this principle, or all revealed laws agree on it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r12.anchor: وقيل : إن ( سواء ) مصدر بمعنى مستوية أي لا يختلف فيها التوراة والانجيل والقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r13.claim: The majority reading makes sawāʾ genitive as an adjective of kalimah; another reading puts it in the accusative as a cognate adverb.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r13.anchor: وهو في قراءظة الجمهور مجرور على أنه نعت لكلمة وقري بنصبه على المصدر +

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r14.claim: The phrase “between us and you” depends on sawāʾ.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r15.claim: “That we worship only God” means that both parties affirm His oneness in worship and devote worship exclusively to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r15.anchor: بأن نوحده بالعبادة ونخلص فيها وفي موضع ( أن )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r16.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r16.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ gives two parses for an lā naʿbuda: genitive as an appositive to kalimah, or nominative as predicate of an omitted subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r16.anchor: كما قال أبو الابقاء الأول الجر على البدلية من ( كلمة ) والثاني الرفع على الخبرية لمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r17.claim: If an did not govern the clause, it could be explanatory; another parse completes the sentence at sawāʾ and makes the following prepositional phrase the predicate before an lā naʿbuda as subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r17.anchor: ولو لا عمل ( أن ) لجاز أن تكون تفسيرية وقيل : إن الكلام تم على ( سواء ) ثم استؤنف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r18.claim: Not associating anything means neither assigning another being a share in the right to worship nor considering it worthy of worship; this is more likely foundational than mere repetition, though some call it emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r18.anchor: لا نجعل غيره شريكا له في استحقاق العبادة ولا نراه أهلا لأن يعبد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r19.claim: The interpretation “we associate no thing from among forms of idolatry” is very remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r19.anchor: وقيل : المراد ( لانشرك به شيئا ) من الشرك وهو بعيد جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r20.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r20.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains taking one another as lords as obeying one another in disobedience to God; the ḥadīth of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim supports this.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r20.anchor: قاله ابن جريج ويؤيده ما أخرجه الترمذي وحسنه من حديث عدي بن حاتم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r21.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r21.claim: In a ḥasan report, ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim says they did not worship their religious authorities; the Prophet explained that they followed them when they made lawful and unlawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r21.anchor: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله فقال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : أما كانوا يحللون لكم ويحرمون

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r22.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r22.claim: ʿIkrimah says taking one another as lords refers to some people prostrating to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r22.anchor: وعن عكرمة أن هذا الاتخاذ هو سجود بعضهم لبعض

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r23.claim: Another interpretation points to Jewish belief that Ezra is God's son and Christian belief that Christ is God's son.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r23.anchor: وقيل : هو مثل اعتقاد اليهود في عزير أنه ابن الله واعتقاد النصارى في المسيح نحو ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r24.claim: The pronoun “our” refers to people, not to all possible beings such as idols, since the People of the Book did not worship idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r24.anchor: وضمير نا على كل تقدير للناس لا للممكن وإن أمكن حتى يشمل الأصنام لأن أهل الكتاب لم يعبدوها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r25.claim: The wording “some of us” hints that the authorities are members of the same human kind as their followers, so cannot be their lords.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r25.anchor: وفي التعبير بالبعض نكتة وهي الإشارة إلى أنهم بعض من جنسنا فكيف يكونون اربابا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r26.claim: An objection says the addressees made others gods alongside God rather than instead of Him; the response takes “besides God” to mean apart from God alone, or says shirk cannot rationally coexist with acknowledging His lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r26.anchor: إن المخاطبين لم يتخذوا البعض أربابا من دون الله بل اتخدوهم آلهة معه سبحانه ( أجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r27.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Christians have the greatest share in the prohibitions listed here.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193/r27.anchor: وللنصارى سود الله تعالى حظهنم الحظ الأوفر من هذه المنهيات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r1.claim: One explanation says that turning away means refusing agreement with the shared message of the revealed books and messengers after it is presented; the proof is then established against them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r1.anchor: المراد فان تولوا عن موافقتكم فيما ذكر مما اتفق عليه الكتب والرسل بعد عرضه عليهم فاعلموا أنهم لزمتهم الحجة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r2.claim: On this reading they refuse out of obstinacy, and “be witnesses” challenges them to acknowledge the truth or indirectly exposes their refusal.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r2.anchor: وإنما أبو اعنادا فقولوا لهم : أنصفوا واعترفوا بأنا على الدين الحق وهو تعجيز لهم أو هو تعريض بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r3.claim: Some verifiers prefer the interpretation that calling them to witness their Islam indirectly makes them admit they are not Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب بعض المحققين وقيل : المراد فان تولوا فقولوا : إنا لا نتحاشى عن الاسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r4.claim: Another view reads the reply as declaring that Muslims do not shrink from Islam or fear anyone and do not conceal their faith as the addressees conceal their unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r4.anchor: فإنا لا نخفي إسلامنا كمت أنكم تخافون وتخفون كفركم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this interpretation fits hypocrites among the People of the Book, who hide from fear, but not these openly professing opponents.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r5.anchor: إنما يحسن لو كان الكلام في منافقي أهل الكتاب لان المنافقين هم الدين يخافون فيخفون

ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r6.claim: Tawallaw is a past-tense verb here; reading it as tatwallaw would misalign the address and leave no valid response, since faqulū addresses the Prophet and believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p193#2/r6.anchor: ( وتولوا ) هنا ماض ولا يجوز أن يكون التقدير تتولوا لفساد المعنى لان ( فقولوا ) خطاب للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والمؤمنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r3.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r3.claim: The exegetes say Najran's Christian delegation met Jews in Medina, each claiming Abraham as a member of its faith; the Prophet denied both claims and called them to Islam, after which both groups accused him of seeking their worship or deification.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: قدم وفد نجران المدينة فالتقوا مع اليهود فاختصموا في إبراهيم عليه السلام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r4.claim: The Arabs call any story that has an explanation a kalima, which is why the revealed call is termed a word.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r4.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل قصة لها شرح كلمة ومنه سميت القصيدة كلمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r5.claim: Sawāʾ means just and equal, a level matter, and also the middle of anything; it is a verbal noun used adjectivally and so does not inflect for gender or number.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r5.anchor: {سواء} عدل بيننا وبينكم مستوية، أي أمر مستو يقال: دعا فلان إلى السواء، أي إلى النصفة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r6.claim: The middle is called just because the fairest and best matters are centered; when sawāʾ has a fatḥa it is lengthened, and with kasra or ḍamma it is shortened.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r6.anchor: وإنما قيل للنصف سواء لأن أعدل الأمور وأفضلها أوسطها وسواء نعت لكلمة إلا أنه مصدر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r7.claim: One parsing makes the clause 'that we worship' nominative by supplying an implied 'it is'; the clause then explains the word.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p49/r7.anchor: ومحل أن رفع على إضمار هي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r1.claim: The continuation gives a nominative parse at the beginning of a sentence, alongside an accusative analysis after an omitted preposition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r1.anchor: رفع بالابتداء، وقيل: محله نصب بنزع حرف الصفة معناه بأن لا نعبد إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r2.claim: Another grammatical analysis treats 'that we worship God alone' as a genitive appositive to 'word.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r2.anchor: وقيل: محله خفض بدلا من الكلمة أي تعالوا إلى أن لا نعبد إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r3.claim: The prohibition on taking one another as lords condemns the Jews' and Christians' practice, linked to the verse about taking rabbis and monks as lords.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r3.anchor: كما فعلت اليهود والنصارى، قال الله تعالى: " اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r4.claim: ʿIkrima interprets taking one another as lords as bowing down to one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو سجود بعضهم لبعض، أي لا تسجدوا لغير الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r5.claim: Another interpretation forbids obeying anyone in disobedience to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا نطيع أحدا في معصية الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r6.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, Muslims are to tell them to witness that they are sincere in exclusive monotheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r6.anchor: {فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا} فقولوا أنتم لهم اشهدوا {بأنا مسلمون} مخلصون بالتوحيد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r7.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r7.claim: Abu Sufyan recounts Heraclius summoning Quraysh merchants during the truce and reading Muhammad's letter, which calls him to Islam and warns him of responsibility if he refuses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r7.anchor: أخبره أن أبا سفيان بن حرب أخبره أن هرقل أرسل إليه في ركب من قريش، وكانوا تجارا بالشام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r8.claim: The Prophet's letter warns Heraclius that refusing Islam leaves him responsible for the Ariīsīn's sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p50/r8.anchor: فإن توليت فإنما عليك إثم الأريسيين

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r1.claim: The address “People of the Book” includes both scriptural communities; it is also said to mean the Najran delegation or the Jews of Medina.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r1.anchor: يعم أهل الكتابين. وقيل يريد به وفد نجران، أو يهود المدينة

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r2.claim: The shared word is a principle on which messengers and scriptures agree, and the following clauses explain it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r2.anchor: لا يختلف فيها الرسل والكتب ويفسرها ما بعدها

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r3.claim: Worship God alone means affirming His unity in worship and devoting worship sincerely to Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r4.claim: Associating nothing with God means neither making anything His partner in deserving worship nor regarding anything else as worthy of worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r4.anchor: ولا نجعل غيره شريكا له في استحقاق العبادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r5.claim: Taking one another as lords includes calling Ezra or the Messiah God’s son and obeying religious scholars in innovations about what is lawful or forbidden, although they are fellow humans.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r5.anchor: ولا نطيع الأحبار فيما أحدثوا من التحريم والتحليل

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r6.claim: The source links the discussion to 9:31; ʿAdi ibn Hatim said they did not worship their clergy, and the Prophet replied that following their rulings on lawful and forbidden was precisely that.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r6.anchor: قال عدي بن حاتم: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.claim: If they turn away from monotheism, the Muslims should say that the evidence has bound them and they must acknowledge the Muslims’ submission.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.anchor: فإن تولوا } عن التوحيد. { فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that the People of the Book should acknowledge that the Muslims are Muslim while they are not.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that they should admit they reject what the scriptures state and the messengers affirm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.anchor: أو اعترفوا بأنكم كافرون بما نطقت به الكتب

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.claim: The argument proceeds gradually: it explains how Jesus’ life stages contradict divinity, answers doubts, invites them to mutual imprecation, then returns to an easier appeal based on Jesus, the Gospel, the prophets, and scriptures; when even that fails, it calls for public acknowledgment of Muslim faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.anchor: من المبالغة في الإرشاد وحسن التدرج في الحجاج

SULAMI:v1p101#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says the just word is the manifestation of servanthood while beholding God's self-sufficiency.
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : هو إظهار العبودية عند ملاحظة الصمدية .

SULAMI:v1p101#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r2.claim: Ibn Ata identifies the just word with realizing divine unity.
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : هو تحقيق التوحيد .

SULAMI:v1p101#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r3.claim: Abu Uthman says worship requires turning one's inner gaze only to the One worshipped and turning to no other in any matter, lest one take another as a lord.
SULAMI:v1p101#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أعلمك طريق التعبد في هذه الآية ، وهو أن لا تطالع بسرك عند اشتغالك العبادة سوى معبودك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r1.claim: After the People of the Book withdrew from the challenge of mutual imprecation, having been silenced by arguments and accepting humiliation and tribute, the Prophet is told to restate the conclusion gently because he longs to guide people.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r1.anchor: ولما نكصوا عن المباهلة بعد أن أورد عليهم أنواع الحجج فانقطعوا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r2.claim: The invitation extends to Christians, Jews, and all other scriptural communities, and proposes a truth established by proofs without claiming a privilege over them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r2.anchor: يدعو دعاء يشمل المحاجين من النصارة وغيرهم ممن له كتاب من اليهود وغيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r3.claim: The Prophet first embraces for himself what he asks of them, a teaching shared by the revealed books and the messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r3.anchor: بدأ بمباشرة ما دعاهم إليه ورضى لهم ما رضي لنفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r4.claim: Calling them People of the Book is tactful because it invokes the knowledge they possess.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r4.anchor: تلطفا بهم بما يحبون فقال : { ياأهل الكتاب } إشارة إلى ما عندهم في ذلك من العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r5.claim: Come means rise out of the lesser and greater forms of polytheism in which they live.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r5.anchor: ارفعوا أنفسكم من حضيض الشرك الأصغر والأكبر الذي أنتم به

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r6.claim: The proposed common word is equitable and contains no unfairness or excess.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r6.anchor: ذات عدل لا شطط فيه بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r7.claim: Exclusive worship of God follows from His possession of all attributes of perfection.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r8.claim: Rejecting partners also forbids believing God has a partner even when that partner is not worshipped.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r8.anchor: لا نعتقد له شريكا وإن لم نعبده

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r9.claim: Taking one another as lords includes figures such as Ezra, Christ, rabbis, and monks who declare things lawful or forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r9.anchor: كعزير والمسيح والأحبار والرهبان الذين يحلون ويحرمون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r10.claim: Since lord can mean a teacher or nurturer, the prohibited claim is to believe a creature acts independently in what belongs uniquely to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r10.anchor: نبه على أن المحذور إنما هو اعتقاد الاستبداد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r11.claim: If they turn away from Islamic monotheism, Muslims must state their disagreement; the apparently peaceful dismissal carries a severe warning of confrontation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r11.anchor: فإن تولوا } أي عن الإسلام له في التوحيد { فقولوا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r12.claim: The conditional wording signals that turning away from this just invitation is hardly likely.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109/r12.anchor: بالتتعبير بأداة الشك إلى أن الإعراض عن هذا العدل لا يكاد يكون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r1.claim: Muslims answer by following Abraham, who declared submission to the Lord of the worlds, and by fulfilling his testament to die only as Muslims.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r2.claim: The response invokes Abraham's submission and testament, cited from 2:131 and 2:132.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r2.anchor:
{ أسلمت لرب العالمين } ) 77
[ البقرة : 131 ] وامتثالا لوصيته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r3.claim: Muslims say they are surrendered to God's command, and the author presents the wording as an implicit warning that the Prophet may soon be ordered to fight them, as messengers customarily did.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r3.anchor: متصفون بالإسلام منقادون لأمره , فيوشك أن يأمرنا نبيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r4.claim: The Muslims' declaration resembles the disciples' testimony; relying on God, they would confront the opponents, who know the past victories and campaigns.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r4.anchor: بما أجاب به الحواريون المشهدون بأنهم مسلمون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r5.claim: The People of the Book knew Arabs loved their forefather Abraham and that Muhammad brought Abraham's religion, as stated at 2:135.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r5.anchor: ما جبل عليه العرب من محبة أبيهم إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r6.claim: The author connects this appeal to the claim that Muhammad brought the upright religion of Abraham, citing 2:135.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p109#2/r6.anchor: بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p110/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p110/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p110/r1.claim: A group of their leaders met before the Prophet; each accused the other and schemed to draw Muslims into error by claiming Abraham followed their religion, although their scriptures do not say this.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p110/r1.anchor: اجتمع ملأ من قرابتهم بحضرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , وضلل كل منهم الآخر

TUSTARI:3:64/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r1.claim: The call to a common word invites the People of the Book to an equitable hope: since they already acknowledge God as Creator, they should worship Him alone.
TUSTARI:3:64/r1.anchor: لأنهم كانوا مقرين بأن خالقهم وخالق السماوات والأرض هو الله تعالى، فنوحده ولا نعبد إلا إياه

TUSTARI:3:64/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r2.claim: Worship is tawhid together with lawful eating and refraining from harming others; lawful consumption and avoiding harm depend on one another.
TUSTARI:3:64/r2.anchor: وأصل العبادة: التوحيد مع أكل الحلال وكف الأذى، ولا يحصل الأكل الحلال إلا بكف الأذى

TUSTARI:3:64/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r3.claim: People should learn lawful food, avoiding harm, and intention in deeds as they learn the Opening, so faith, hearts, and limbs become pure; these are fundamentals.
TUSTARI:3:64/r3.anchor: وأن تعلموا أكل الحلال وترك أذى الخلق والنية في الأعمال كما تعلموا فاتحة الكتاب، ليصفوا إيمانكم وقلوبكم وجوارحكم

TUSTARI:3:64/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r4.speaker: الثوري
TUSTARI:3:64/r4.claim: Al-Thawri compares the servant's profession of “there is no god but God” to water in the world, citing that every living thing is made from water.
TUSTARI:3:64/r4.anchor: حكى محمد بن سوار عن الثوري أنه قال: منزلة لا إله إلا الله في العبد بمنزلة الماء في الدنيا

TUSTARI:3:64/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r5.claim: A person who gains no benefit from professing tawhid and following the Prophet's Sunna is spiritually dead.
TUSTARI:3:64/r5.anchor: فمن لم ينفعه اعتقاد لا إله إلا الله والاقتداء بسنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو ميت

TUSTARI:3:64/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r6.claim: Sahl recounts a saint asking God to forgive a crucified man who had professed tawhid; by God's power the man's body turned toward the qibla.
TUSTARI:3:64/r6.anchor: اجتاز برجل مصلوب وجهه إلى غير القبلة، فقال: أين ذلك اللسان الذي كنت تقول به صادقا

TUSTARI:3:64/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r7.claim: The third aspect is bodily obedience done sincerely for God, including prayer, almsgiving, contentment, and acceptance; this calls people to the best speech and deeds.
TUSTARI:3:64/r7.anchor: والثالث إطاعة بالجوارح خالصا لله، من إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والقنوع والرضا

TUSTARI:3:64/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:64/r8.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:64/r8.claim: Faith in God and the Quran calls people to acknowledge divine lordship and worship God in distress; this lets prophets recognize who responds.
TUSTARI:3:64/r8.anchor: لم تعرف الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام من أجابهم من الخلق

DURR-FULL:v2p233/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r7.speaker: أبو سفيان
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r7.claim: Abu Sufyan recounts that the Prophet's letter to Heraclius invited him to Islam, promised a double reward if he accepted, warned of the sin of the Arisiyyin if he turned away, and quoted the common-word passage.
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حدثني أبو سفيان أن هرقل دعا بكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأه فإذا فيه: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v2p233/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's letter to unbelievers quoted the invitation to a common word.
DURR-FULL:v2p233/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الكفار {تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم} الآية

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the Prophet invited the Jews of Medina to the common word; they refused and he fought them until they paid jizya.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {تعالوا إلى كلمة} الآية قال: بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا يهود أهل المدينة إلى ذلك فأبوا عليه

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r2.claim: The Prophet called the Jews of Medina to the common word because they disputed over Abraham and claimed he died a Jew; God disproved their claim in 3:65.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا يهود أهل المدينة إلى الكلمة السواء وهم الذين حاجوا في إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r3.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the Prophet invited the Jews to the common word.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r3.anchor: عن الربيع قال: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا اليهود إلى الكلمة السواء

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r4.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r4.claim: The Prophet invited the Najran delegation to a fair, middle position that left them without an argument.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير في قوله {قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا} الآية قال: فدعاهم إلى النصف وقطع عنهم الحجة يعني وفد نجران

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r5.claim: The Prophet called the Christian delegation from Najran to the common word.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r5.anchor: عن السدي قال: ثم دعاهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعني الوفد من نصارى نجران فقال {يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء}

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r6.claim: Qatada explains “sawāʾ” as justice or equity.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء} قال: عدل

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r7.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r7.claim: Al-Rabi likewise explains “sawāʾ” as justice or equity.

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “sawāʾ” as justice and cites an unnamed poet's use of the word as evidence of Arabic usage.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {سواء بيننا وبينكم} قال: عدل قال: وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال: نعم أما سمعت قول الشاعر
