DURR-FULL:v2p234/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r9.claim: The common word is the declaration that there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r9.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: كلمة السواء لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r10.claim: Mujahid likewise explains the common word as the declaration that there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد {تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء} قال: لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r11.claim: Not taking people as lords means not obeying one another in disobedience to God; this form of lordship is obedience to leaders in matters outside worship, even without prostrating to them.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r11.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله} قال: لا يطيع بعضنا بعضا في معصية الله

DURR-FULL:v2p234/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r12.claim: Ikrima interprets taking people as lords as some people prostrating to others.
DURR-FULL:v2p234/r12.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا} قال: سجود بعضهم لبعض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r1.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to the Roman ruler, identifying “People of the Book” as Jews and Christians.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r1.anchor: ان عمر بن عبد العزيز كتب الي اليون طاغية الروم قال : فيما انزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قل يا اهل الكتاب يعني اليهود والنصارى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r2.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r2.claim: Abū Sufyān recounts the Prophet's letter to Heraclius: it called him to Islam and worship of God alone, promised a double reward for accepting, and warned of the consequence of refusal.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r2.anchor: أبا سفيان بن حرب اخبره ان هرقل دعا بكتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فان فيه : من محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the Prophet invited the Jews of Medina to worship God alone; they refused, and he fought them until they accepted the jizya.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ان لا نعبد الا الله قال : بلغني ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا يهود اهل المدينة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the equitable word as “there is no god but God.”
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r4.anchor: ثنا الربيع بن انس قال أبو العالية : كلمة السواء لا اله الا الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes the call as an invitation to Islam that the People of the Book refused.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r5.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : يا اهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة قال : دعوا الاسلام فابوا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the call invited them to an equitable middle position and thereby cut off their argument.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p669#2/r6.anchor: قال محمد ابن اسحاق تعالوا إلى كلمة قال : دعاهم إلى النصف وقطع عنهم الحجة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r1.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains “equitable between us and you” as just between both parties.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r1.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : قل يا اهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم يقول : عدل بيننا وبينكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r2.speaker: عكررمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the “lords” taken besides God are idols.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r2.anchor: عن عكررمة في قوله : اربابا يعني الاصنام .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says lordship can mean people obeying their masters and leaders in matters outside worship.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج قوله : اربابا من دون الله قال : يقال : ان الربوبية ان يطيع الناس سادتهم وقادتهم في غير عبادة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r4.claim: ʿIkrima also interprets taking one another as lords as people prostrating to one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p670/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا اربابا من دون الله قال : سجود بعضهم لبعض .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r1.claim: The first manifestation of Islam's reform is purifying belief from doubt, deception, superstition, and illusion, grounding submission in one great God and His complete attributes, and unifying people's moral starting point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r1.anchor: المظهر الأول : إصلاح العقيدة بحمل الذهن على اعتقاد لا يشوبه تردد ولا تمويه ولا أوهام ولا خرافات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r2.claim: Islam began with reforming belief because sound thought begins every reform; deviant belief creates groundless fears and desires, while sound belief enables other improvement because a person is a soul rather than a body.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r2.anchor: وكان إصلاح الإعتقاد أهم ما ابتدأ به الإسلام ، وأكثر ما تعرض له ؛ وذلك لأن إصلاح الفكرة هو مبدأ كل إصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r3.claim: Islamic belief gives rise to self-respect, independence of judgment, freedom of thought, and human equality apart from differences in virtue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r3.anchor: ثم نشأ عن هذا الإعتقاد الإسلامي : عزة النفس ، وأصلة الرأي ، وحرية العقل ، ومساواة الناس فيما عدا الفضائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r4.claim: Islam explains creed more fully than any other religion; even many sound religions say little about the Creator's attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r4.anchor: وقد أكثر الإسلام شرح العقائد إكثارا لا يشبهه فيه دين آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r5.claim: A second manifestation combines purification of the soul with organizing life through law; most religions focus on sermons and worship, while the Qur'an repeatedly joins both benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r5.anchor: المظهر الثاني : جمعه بين إصلاح النفوس ، بالتزكية ، وبين إصلاح نظام الحياة ، بالتشريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r6.claim: The Qur'an pairs belief and righteous action, citing the promise of a good life and reward for believing men and women who act righteously.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p194/r6.anchor: قال تعالى : { من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r1.claim: The passage resumes debate after the invitation to mutual imprecation, driven by the Prophet's concern for their faith and pointing to the People of the Book's deviation from true submission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r1.anchor: رجوع إلى المجادلة ، بعد انقطاعها بالدعاء إلى المباهلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r2.claim: The argument presses them to worship God alone and abandon the doctrine that assigns divinity to another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r2.anchor: دعوتهم إلى تخصيص الله بالعبادة ونبذ عقيدة إشراك غيره في الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r3.claim: The address repeats the call of 3:61 in a new argument: the earlier verse exposed their weak confidence, this verse asserts Islam's truth, so no conjunction links them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r3.anchor: صحة عقيدة الإسلام ، ولذلك لم تعطف هذه الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r4.claim: Here the People of the Book means Christians, since they made a created being their lord and worshipped him alongside God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r4.anchor: والمراد بأهل الكتاب هنا النصارى : لأنهم هم الذين اتخذوا المخلوق ربا وعبدوه مع الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r5.claim: Come is a metaphorical invitation to gather around an agreed word, treating that word as a place where people meet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r5.anchor: تمثيل : جعلت الكلمة المجتمع عليها بشبه المكان المراد الاجتماع عنده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r6.claim: Word means a brief utterance, as in the verse about the speaker's final word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r6.anchor: الكلمة هنا أطلقت على الكلام الوجيز كما في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r7.claim: The commentators explain equal as justice or as a moderate position free of excess; both senses derive from a level, middle place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r7.anchor: قيل بمعنى العدل ، وقيل بمعنى قصد لا شطط فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes equal to mean a principle shared by all people, a good interpretation because making some people lords over others is unequal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : بمعنى ما يستوي فيه جميع الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r9.claim: Equal is a verbal noun used adjectivally for the feminine word, so it does not take feminine agreement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r9.anchor: فالسواء غير مؤنث ، وصف به { كلمة } ، وهو لفظ مؤنث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r10.claim: The clause that we worship none but God is an appositive explaining the word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r10.anchor: و { ألا نعبد } بدل من { كلمة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r11.speaker: جماعة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r11.claim: A group instead parses the clause that we worship none but God as an appositive to equal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r11.anchor: وقال جماعة : هو بدل من سواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r12.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r12.claim: Ibn Hisham rejects the group's parsing of the clause as an appositive to equal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r12.anchor: ورده ابن هشام ، في النوع الثاني من الجهة السادسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r13.speaker: الدماميني وغيره
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p268/r13.claim: Al-Damamini and others object to Ibn Hisham's rejection of that parsing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r1.claim: The appositive-to-equal parsing is rejected by grammatical convention, not meaning: it would make the clause function like an unsuitable adjective of the word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r1.anchor: والحق أنه مردود من جهة مراعاة الاصطلاح لا من جهة المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r2.claim: The pronoun in between us refers contextually to the Prophet and the Muslims, as the following command to testify confirms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r2.anchor: وضمير بيننا عائد على معلوم من المقام : وهو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r3.claim: The call to worship God alone indirectly rebukes all who worship Christ.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r4.claim: The conditional particle if presents their turning away as unlikely after this proof and the preceding evidence, yet hypothetically possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r4.anchor: جيء في هذا الشرط بحرف إن لأن التولي بعد نهوض هذه الحجة وما قبلها من الأدلة غريب الوقوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r5.claim: If they still turn away, Muslims should give up hope of their conversion, disengage while maintaining Islam, and testify so their refusal cannot be mistaken for Muslim weakness or concession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p269/r5.anchor: فقد صاروا بحيث يؤيس من إسلامهم فأعرضوا عنهم ، وأمسكوا أنتم بإسلامكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p270/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p270/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p270/r3.claim: The transition follows the warning to testify to Islam if they turn away: Muhammad's Islam was publicly linked with Abraham's hanif religion among Meccan polytheists, Jews, and Najran Christians.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p270/r3.anchor: أن الإسلام الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يرجع إلى الحنيفية دين إبراهيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r8.speaker: قتادة والربيع وابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r8.claim: They say the Prophet invited the Jews of Medina, who had disputed about Abraham, to the common word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r8.anchor: فقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رسول الله عليه السلام دعا يهود المدينة إلى الكلمة السواء، وهم الذين حاجوا في إبراهيم، وقاله الربيع وابن جريج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r9.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr and al-Suddī say the verse was revealed about the delegation from Najran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r9.anchor: وقال محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: نزلت الآية في وفد نجران، وقاله السدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says that after the people of Najran refused the mutual imprecation, they were invited to the easier proposal of the common word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r10.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: لما أبى أهل نجران ما دعوا إليه من الملاعنة، دعوا إلى أيسر من ذلك وهي «الكلمة السواء»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors revelation about Najran, while taking ‘People of the Book’ to include all Christians and Jews.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r11.anchor: والذي يظهر لي أن الآية نزلت في وفد نجران، لكن لفظ أهل الكتاب يعمهم وسواهم من النصارى واليهود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r12.claim: The Prophet later used the verse with Medina’s Jews, wrote it to Heraclius, and should invite the People of the Book by it until the Last Day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r12.anchor: فدعا النبي عليه السلام بعد ذلك يهود المدينة بالآية، وكذلك كتب بها إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r13.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r13.claim: Most readers pronounce kalima with a fatḥa on kāf and kasra on lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r13.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «إلى كلمة» بفتح الكاف وكسر اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r14.speaker: أبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r14.claim: Abū al-Sammāl is reported to read kalima with a fatḥa on kāf and a still lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r14.anchor: وروى أبو السمال: «كلمة» بفتح الكاف وسكون اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r15.speaker: أبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r15.claim: A second reading attributed to Abū al-Sammāl has kasra on kāf and a still lām, by shifting the lām’s vowel as in kabid/kabd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r15.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قرأ «كلمة» بكسر الكاف وسكون اللام، وذلك على إلقاء حركة اللام على الكاف كما قالوا في كبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r16.claim: Here kalima denotes expressions containing the meanings being invited to; Arabs also call a whole poem a ‘word.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r16.anchor: و «الكلمة» هنا عبارة عن الألفاظ التي تتضمن المعاني المدعو إليها، وهي ما فسره بعد ذلك بقوله ألا نعبد الآية وهذا كما تسمي العرب القصيدة كلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r17.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r17.claim: Most exegetes take ‘the word’ to be the proposal explained in the following clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p448/r17.anchor: وجمهور المفسرين على أن الكلمة هي ما فسر بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the common word as ‘There is no god but God.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r2.speaker: قتادة والربيع وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r2.claim: They gloss sawāʾ as a word of justice, and Ibn Masʿūd’s codex reads ‘a word of justice between us and you.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r2.anchor: قال قتادة والربيع وغيرهما: معناه إلى كلمة عدل، فهذا معنى «السواء» ، وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: «إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r3.claim: Some exegetes understand sawāʾ as a word of right purpose or direction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: معناه إلى كلمة قصد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers the ‘right purpose’ gloss close in meaning to the preceding gloss of justice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r4.anchor: وهذا قريب في المعنى من الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r5.claim: He proposes that sawāʾ here means shared principles on which all people, young and old, stand equally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r5.anchor: دعاهم إلى معان جميع الناس فيها مستوون، صغيرهم وكبيرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r6.claim: This appeal suits human nature because the invitees had made unequal relations by taking one another as lords.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r6.anchor: وقد كانت سيرة المدعوين أن يتخذ بعضهم بعضا أربابا فلم يكونوا على استواء حال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r7.claim: He distinguishes equal standing from justice alone: an enslaved captive ordered to convert or die is treated justly, but not as an equal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r7.anchor: والفرق بين هذا التفسير وبين تفسير اللفظة بعدل، أنك لو دعوت أسيرا عندك إلى أن يسلم أو تضرب عنقه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r8.claim: Inviting a captive to faith, freedom, and an equal share in life exemplifies equality of status, his preferred sense of sawāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r8.anchor: ولو دعوت أسيرك إلى أن يؤمن فيكون حرا مقاسما لك في عيشك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r9.claim: All readings retain a sense of justice, but he finds the equality-of-status sense unattested in earlier exegetes and persuasive because souls welcome it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r9.anchor: واللفظة على كل تأويل فيها معنى العدل، ولكني لم أر لمتقدم أن يكون في اللفظة معنى قصد استواء الحال، وهو عندي حسن، لأن النفوس تألفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r10.claim: He links this sense to the phrase ‘on equal terms’ in 8:58 under one interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا الحد جاءت لفظة سواء في قوله تعالى: فانبذ إليهم على سواء [الأنفال: 58] على بعض التأويلات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r11.claim: The clause ‘that we worship’ may be genitive after ilā as an apposition to kalima, or nominative as its predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r11.anchor: وقوله ألا نعبد يحتمل أن يكون في موضع خفض بمعنى، إلى ألا نعبد، فذلك على البدل من كلمة ويحتمل أن يكون في موضع رفع بمعنى، هي ألا نعبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r12.speaker: المهدوي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r12.claim: Al-Mahdawī and others offer additional possible parses, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya says their account is over-elaborate where it entails nominative naʿbud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r12.anchor: وما ذكره المهدوي وغيره من أن تكون مفسرة إلى غير ذلك من الجائزات التي يلزم عنها رفع نعبد إكثار منهم فاختصرته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r13.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r13.claim: ʿIkrima takes making one another lords to its highest degree: believing people divine and worshipping them, as with ʿUzayr and Jesus son of Mary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r13.anchor: أعلاها اعتقادهم فيهم الألوهية، وعبادتهم لهم على ذلك، كعزير وعيسى ابن مريم، وبهذا فسر عكرمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies its lowest degree as obeying bishops and leaders in unbelief and sins and treating that obedience as religious law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r14.anchor: وأدنى ذلك طاعتهم لأساقفتهم ورؤسائهم في كل ما أمروا به من الكفر والمعاصي والتزامهم طاعتهم شرعا، وبهذا فسر ابن جريج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r15.claim: The invitation therefore rejects every such form of lordship and makes God’s command, conveyed by His Prophet, the rule to obey.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r15.anchor: فجاءت الآية بالدعاء إلى ترك ذلك كله وأن يكون الممتثل ما قاله الله تعالى على لسان نبيه عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r16.claim: The command to say ‘bear witness that we are Muslims’ requires openly confronting the rejecters, as reproach and threat over the consequences of turning away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p449/r16.anchor: أمر بتصريح مخالفتهم بمخاطبتهم ومواجهتهم بذلك، وإشهادهم على معنى التوبيخ والتهديد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p106#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p106#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p106#4/r1.claim: Sawāʾ means fairness or equity; it also means the middle, since the middle is the fairest part.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p106#4/r1.anchor: أي: نصف. يقال: دعاك إلى السواء أي إلى النصفة. وسواء كل شيء: وسطه.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r1.speaker: قتادة، ابن جريج، الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r1.claim: One view identifies the addressees as the Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r1.anchor: أحدها انهم اليهود قاله قتادة وابن جريج والربيع بن أنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r2.speaker: السدي، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r2.claim: A second view identifies them as the Najran delegation who debated about Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r2.anchor: والثاني وفد نجران الذين حاجوا في عيسى قاله السدي و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r3.claim: Hasan says the address includes both scriptural communities.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r3.anchor: والثالث أهل الكتابين جميعا قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned priests and monks; the Prophet sent it to Ja'far and his companions in Abyssinia, and Ja'far recited it before the Negus and Abyssinian leaders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس نزلت في القسيسين والرهبان فبعث بها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى جعفر و أصحابه بالحبشة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r5.claim: The exegetes identify the “word” as “there is no god but God.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r5.anchor: فأما الكلمة فقال المفسرون هي لا إله إلا الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r6.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r6.claim: One explanation of the singular “word” is that it can denote a whole discourse or story; Zuhayr's “word” means his poem, and the term “rhyme” can name a whole ode by its last word.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r6.anchor: أحدهما أن الكلمة تعبر عن ألفاظ وكلمات قال اللغويون ومعنى كلمة كلام فيه شرح قصة وإن طال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r7.speaker: الخنساء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r7.claim: The cited verse from al-Khansa calls the ode's rhyme by the singular, illustrating a singular expression for a whole poem.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r7.anchor: قالت الخنساء وقافيه مثل حد السنا ن تبقى ويذهب من قالها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r8.claim: Another explanation is that “word” stands for “words,” using a singular where a plural is intended, as in Alqama's verse about hides.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p400#4/r8.anchor: والثاني أن المراد بالكلمة كلمات فاكتفى بالكلمة من كلمات كما قال علقمة بن عبدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says sawaʾ means justice, deriving from equality; the term has three vowelled forms, and Zuhayr's verse uses it in this sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج يعني بالسواء العدل وهو من استواء الشئ ويقال للعدل سواء وسواء وسواء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r2.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r2.claim: Zuhayr's poem uses sawaʾ for equity between two parties.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r2.anchor: قال زهير بن أبي سلمى أروني خطة لاضيم فيها يسوي بيننا فيها السواء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r3.claim: The clause “that we worship none but God” may be genitive as an apposition to “word,” meaning come to not worshiping anyone but God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r3.anchor: وموضع أن في قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا تعبدوا إلا الله ﴾ خفض على البدل من كلمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r4.claim: Alternatively, the clause may be nominative as the answer to the implied question, “What is the word?”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r4.anchor: وجائز أن يكون أن في موضع رفع كأن قائلا قال ما الكلمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r5.claim: One interpretation of not taking one another as lords is forbidding people to prostrate to one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r5.anchor: أحدها أن سجود بعضهم لبعض قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r6.claim: A second interpretation forbids obeying one another in disobedience to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r6.anchor: والثاني لا يطيع بعضنا بعضا في معصية الله قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r7.speaker: مقاتل، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r7.claim: A third interpretation forbids making anyone besides God a lord, as Christians did with the Messiah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p401/r7.anchor: والثالث أن نجعل غير الله ربا كما قالت النصارى في المسيح قاله مقاتل و الزجاج

MAJAZ:v1p95/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p95/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p95/r10.claim: Sawāʾ baynanā wa-baynakum means fairness or an equal position; the idiom “he invited you to equality” means accept his offer.
MAJAZ:v1p95/r10.anchor: «سواء بيننا وبينكم» (64) أي النصف، يقال: قد دعاك إلى السواء فاقبل منه.

MAJAZ:v1p96/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p96/r1.claim: The phrase “a word” is explained by the following words about worshipping God alone and not associating anything with Him.
MAJAZ:v1p96/r1.anchor: «إلى كلمة» (64) مفسرة بعد «ألا نعبد إلا الله، ولا نشرك به شيئا» بهذه الكلمة التي دعاهم إليها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r1.claim: The address includes all People of the Book, Jews, Christians, and those like them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r1.anchor: هذا الخطاب يعم أهل الكتاب من اليهود والنصارى، ومن جرى مجراهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r2.claim: Here kalima means a meaningful sentence, and sawa means justice and fairness in which both sides stand equally.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r2.anchor: والكلمة تطلق على الجملة المفيدة كما قال هاهنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r3.claim: The shared call is to worship God alone and avoid every form of association, including idols, crosses, tyrants, fire, or anything else; all messengers preached this monotheism.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r3.anchor: لا وثنا، ولا صنما، ولا صليبا ولا طاغوتا، ولا نارا، ولا شيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r4.claim: Taking one another as lords means obeying one another in disobedience to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: يعني: يطيع بعضنا بعضا في معصية الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r5.claim: Taking one another as lords means some people prostrate to others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p55/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يعني: يسجد بعضنا لبعض.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r1.claim: If the People of the Book turn away from the fair invitation, believers should testify that they remain upon the Islam God legislated for them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r1.anchor: فإن تولوا عن هذا النصف وهذه الدعوة فأشهدوهم أنتم على استمراركم على الإسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r2.speaker: أبو سفيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account of his audience with Heraclius, Abu Sufyan answered questions about Muhammad while still a polytheist; the meeting occurred after Hudaybiyya and before the conquest, and the Prophet's letter quoted this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r2.anchor: وكان ذلك بعد صلح الحديبية وقبل الفتح، كما هو مصرح به في الحديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others say the opening of Aal Imran through roughly eighty verses was revealed about the Najran delegation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r3.anchor: أن صدر سورة آل عمران إلى بضع وثمانين آية منها نزلت في وفد نجران

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r4.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri says the Najran delegation were the first to offer jizya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r4.anchor: وقال الزهري: هم أول من بذل الجزية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir raises the chronological tension between this verse's inclusion in the letter before the conquest and the report that the jizya verse came after it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r5.anchor: فما الجمع بين كتابة هذه الآية قبل الفتح إلى هرقل في جملة الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r6.claim: One possible reconciliation is that this verse was revealed twice, once before Hudaybiyya and once after the conquest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r6.anchor: يحتمل أن هذه الآية نزلت مرتين، مرة قبل الحديبية، ومرة بعد الفتح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r7.claim: Another possibility is that the opening of Aal Imran through this verse concerned Najran, while this verse itself had already been revealed; the report extending the revelation to more than eighty verses may be unpreserved given Abu Sufyan's hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p56/r7.anchor: ليس بمحفوظ، لدلالة حديث أبي سفيان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r1.claim: A third reconciliation places the Najran delegation before Hudaybiyya and treats their payment as a settlement instead of jizya; the later jizya ruling then matched this precedent, as the shares ruling matched Abdullah ibn Jahsh's pre-Badr expedition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن قدوم وفد نجران كان قبل الحديبية، وأن الذي بذلوه مصالحة عن المباهلة لا على وجه الجزية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r2.claim: A fourth possibility is that the Prophet ordered the wording in his letter before it was revealed, then revelation agreed with it, as it did with Umar's positions on the veil, captives, funeral prayer for hypocrites, and the Station of Abraham.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p57/r2.anchor: كما نزل بموافقة عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه في الحجاب وفي الأسارى

NAHHAS:v1p382/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r17.speaker: قعنب
NAHHAS:v1p382/r17.claim: Quʿnub reads كلمة with the lām’s vowel shifted onto the kāf, like كبد.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r17.anchor: وقرأ قعنب ( كلمة ) ألقى حركة اللام على الكاف كما يقال كبد

NAHHAS:v1p382/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r18.speaker: أبو العالية
NAHHAS:v1p382/r18.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the “word” is لا إله إلا الله.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r18.anchor: قال أبو العالية الكلمة لا إله إلا الله

NAHHAS:v1p382/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p382/r19.claim: سواء is an adjective of كلمة; al-Ḥasan instead reads سواءا in the accusative as a cognate accusative meaning “in equal measure.”
NAHHAS:v1p382/r19.anchor: ( سواء ) نعت لكلمة وقرأ الحسن ( سواءا ) بالنصب أي استوت استواءا

NAHHAS:v1p382/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r21.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p382/r21.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says سوى and سوى can mean justice and cites ʿAbd Allāh’s codex reading عدل in place of سواء.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r21.anchor: قال الفراء ويقال في معنى العدل سوى وسوى قال وفي قراءة عبد الله ( إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم )

NAHHAS:v1p382/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p382/r22.claim: ألا نعبد إلا الله can be an apposition explaining كلمة, or be understood with an implied هي.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r22.anchor: ( ألا نعبد إلا الله ) على البدل من كلمة وإن شئت كان التقدير هي أن لا نعبد إلا الله

NAHHAS:v1p382/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r23.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v1p382/r23.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allow jussive verbs after ألا by attraction to an understood أن at the beginning.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r23.anchor: قال الكسائي والفراء ويجوز ( ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا ) بالجزم على التوهم إنه ليس في أول الكلام أن

NAHHAS:v1p382/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p382/r24.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says grammatical “attraction by supposition” yields nothing; following Sībawayh, the verbs can be jussive after explanatory أن meaning أي, or raised as predicates.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r24.anchor: قال أبو جعفر التوهم لا يحصل منه شيء ولكن مذهب سيبويه أنه يجوز في نعبد وما بعده الجزم

NAHHAS:v1p382/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p382/r25.claim: The clause can also be raised with the sense that they do not worship God alone; this is compared with أن لا يرجع إليهم قولا.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r25.anchor: ويجوز على هذا أن يرفع نعبد وما بعده ويكون خبرا ويجوز الرفع بمعنى أنه لا نعبد

NAHHAS:v1p382/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p382/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p382/r26.claim: Not taking one another as lords means not worshipping Jesus, who is human like them, or accepting monks’ prohibitions of what God did not forbid.
NAHHAS:v1p382/r26.anchor: لا نعبد عيسى لأنه بشر مثلنا ولا نقبل من الرهبان تحريمهم علينا ما لم يحرمه الله

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r8.claim: Kalima and kalām are synonymous; sawāʾ is the middle of a thing, and may denote the most balanced and best center.
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r8.anchor: الكلمة والكلام واحد. وسواء كل شيء وسطه، ومنه قراءة (فى سواء الجحيم)

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r9.claim: Sawāʾ does not take dual or plural forms; with fatḥa it is long, and with kasra or ḍamma it is short, as in the cited phrase makānan suwā.
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r9.anchor: وسواء لا يثنى ولا يجمع وإذا فتح السين مددت، وإذا كسرت أو ضممت - قصرت

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r13.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r13.claim: The clause an lā naʿbuda may be raised as an implied subject, “it is that we worship,” with sawāʾ describing kalima.

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r14.claim: One parse raises an lā naʿbuda by ellipsis, “it is that we worship,” and makes sawāʾ an adjective of kalima.
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r14.anchor: قوله: ألا نعبد محل (أن) قيل: رفع بإضمار، وتقديره: هي ألا نعبد، ويكون (سواء) صفة ل (كلمة) في اللفظ والمعنى

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r15.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r15.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses an lā naʿbuda as a nominative subject.

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r16.claim: Another parse makes the clause a genitive apposition to kalima, understood as “come to worship God alone.”
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r16.anchor: وقيل: محله خفض على البدل من (كلمة) بتقدير: تعالوا إلى ألا نعبد إلا الله

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r17.claim: A further parse supplies a missing preposition, yielding bi-an lā naʿbuda.
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r17.anchor: وقيل: بنزع حرف الصفة تقديره: بألا نعبد

JISHUMI:v2p1192/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r18.claim: Sawāʾ may mean the midpoint because it is the fairest, best, and most central position.
JISHUMI:v2p1192/r18.anchor: وقيل: للنصف سواء؛ لأنه أعدل الأشياء وأفضلها وأوسطها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r1.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r1.claim: One reported identification says the addressees are the people of both scriptures, Jews and Christians.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r1.anchor: قيل هم أهل الكتابين وقيل وفد نجران وقيل يهود المدينة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r2.claim: Another reported identification says the addressees are the Najran delegation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r2.anchor: قيل هم أهل الكتابين وقيل وفد نجران وقيل يهود المدينة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r3.claim: A third reported identification says the addressees are the Jews of Medina.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r3.anchor: قيل هم أهل الكتابين وقيل وفد نجران وقيل يهود المدينة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r4.claim: The proposed common word is a point of agreement among Muslims, Jews, and Christians, on which the Qur'an, Torah, and Gospel do not differ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r4.anchor: مستوية بيننا وبينكم لا يختلف فيها القرآن والتوراة والإنجيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r5.claim: The common word is exclusive worship of God: it rejects calling Ezra or Christ God's son and rejects obeying rabbis who invent religious prohibitions and permissions apart from God's law.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r5.anchor: يعني تعالوا إليها حتى لا نقول عزير ابن الله ولا المسيح ابن الله لأن كل واحد منهما بعضنا بشر مثلنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r6.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r6.claim: Adi says they had not worshipped their rabbis; the Prophet replies that they accepted the rabbis' decisions to make things lawful or unlawful, and that was their worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r6.anchor: وعن عدي بن حاتم 172 ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله قال ( أليس كانوا يحلون لكم ويحرمون فتأخذون بقولهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r7.speaker: الفضيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r7.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says he sees no difference between obeying a created being against the Creator and praying toward somewhere other than the qibla.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r7.anchor: وعن الفضيل لا أبالي أطعت مخلوقا في معصية الخالق أو صليت لغير القبلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r8.claim: A reading gives كلمة a still lām; al-Hasan reads سواء in the accusative to express equality.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r8.anchor: وقرىء ( كلمة ) بسكون اللام وقرأ الحسن ( سواء ) بالنصب بمعنى استوت استواء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398/r9.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, the command means that they have turned away from monotheism.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r1.claim: The command to testify means the proof has bound the People of the Book, so they must concede that the Muslims are in the right, like a defeated opponent acknowledging the victor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r1.anchor: أي لزمتكم الحجة فوجب عليكم أن تعترفوا وتسلموا بأنا مسلمون دونكم كما يقول الغالب للمغلوب في جدال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, this is an indirect challenge: by turning from manifest truth, they should admit that they are unbelievers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من باب التعريض ومعناه اشهدوا واعترفوا بأنكم كافرون حيث توليتم عن الحق بعد ظهوره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r3.claim: Jews and Christians each claimed Abraham; the reply is that Judaism and Christianity began after their scriptures, long after Abraham's eras, so he could not have belonged to either later religion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r3.anchor: زعم كل فريق من اليهود والنصارى أن إبراهيم كان منهم وجادلوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r4.claim: The rebuke asks whether they will use reason and stop making an impossible argument.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p398#2/r4.anchor: حتى لا تجادلوا مثل هذا الجدال المحال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r1.speaker: الحسن، السدي، ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r1.claim: One view says the address “People of the Book” concerns the Christians of Najran.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r1.anchor: أنهم نصارى نجران , وهذا قول الحسن والسدي وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r2.speaker: قتادة، الربيع، ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r2.claim: Another view identifies the addressees as the Jews of Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r2.anchor: انهم يهود المدينة , وهذا قول قتادة , والربيع , وابن جريح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r3.claim: “Let none of us take others as lords” condemns followers obeying leaders when those leaders command disobedience to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r3.anchor: هو طاعة الاتباع لرؤسائهم في أوامرهم بمعاصي الله , وهذا قول ابن جريح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r4.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r4.claim: Another interpretation of taking people as lords is some people prostrating to others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p399/r4.anchor: سجود بعضهم لبعض , هذا قول عكرمة .

MUQATIL:3:64/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r1.claim: The shared word is justice and sincerity.

MUQATIL:3:64/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r2.claim: The invitation is to worship God alone and associate no created thing with Him.
MUQATIL:3:64/r2.anchor: ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا } من خلقه

MUQATIL:3:64/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r3.claim: Taking one another as lords means the People of the Book took Jesus as a lord.
MUQATIL:3:64/r3.anchor: ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله }؛ لأنهم اتخذوا عيسى ربا

MUQATIL:3:64/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r4.claim: If they refuse monotheism, Muslims should testify that they are sincere in their monotheism.
MUQATIL:3:64/r4.anchor: فإن أبوا التوحيد، { فقولوا } لهم أنتم

MUQATIL:3:64/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r5.speaker: العاقب
MUQATIL:3:64/r5.claim: Al-ʿAqib says there is no point in mutual imprecation: if Muhammad lies, the imprecation will not harm them, but if he is truthful, God will destroy them within a year.
MUQATIL:3:64/r5.anchor: فقال العاقب: ما نصنع بملاعنته شيئا، فو الله لئن كان كاذبا ما ملاعنته بشىء

MUQATIL:3:64/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r6.claim: The delegation proposed a pact allowing Muhammad to campaign without frightening them or diverting them from their religion, in return for payments.
MUQATIL:3:64/r6.anchor: قالوا: يا محمد، نصالحك على أن تغزونا ولا تخيفنا ولا تردنا عن ديننا

MUQATIL:3:64/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r7.claim: The proposed payments were one thousand garments in each of Safar and Rajab and thirty old iron coats of mail.
MUQATIL:3:64/r7.anchor: ألف حلة فى صفر، وألف حلة فى رجب، وعلى ثلاثين درعا من حديد عادية

MUQATIL:3:64/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:64/r8.claim: The Prophet made the proposed agreement with them.
MUQATIL:3:64/r8.anchor: فصالحهم النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم على ذلك

MUQATIL:3:64/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:3:64/r9.claim: The Prophet swore that if they had invoked the curse, the year would not pass with any of them present and God would destroy the liars.
MUQATIL:3:64/r9.anchor: والذى نفس محمد بيده، لولا عنونى ما حال الحول، ويحضرنى منهم أحد، ولأهلك الله الكاذبين

MUQATIL:3:64/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r10.speaker: عمر
MUQATIL:3:64/r10.claim: Umar asked whose hand the Prophet would take if he invoked the curse with them.
MUQATIL:3:64/r10.anchor: قال عمر، رضى الله عنه: لو لاعنتهم بيد من كنت تأخذ

MUQATIL:3:64/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:64/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:3:64/r11.claim: The Prophet said he would take the hands of ʿAli, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Hafsa, and ʿAisha.
MUQATIL:3:64/r11.anchor: آخذ بيد على، وفاطمة، والحسن، والحسين، عليهم السلام، وحفصة، وعائشة، رحمهما الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r1.claim: The People of the Book may mean holders of the two scriptures, the Najran delegation, or the Jews of Medina.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r1.anchor: هم أهل الكتابين أو وفد نجران أو يهود المدينة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r2.claim: The shared, even-handed word is one on which Quran, Torah and Gospel do not differ.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r2.anchor: لا يختلف فيها القرآن والتوراة والإنجيل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r3.claim: The word is to worship God alone, associate nothing with Him, and not make humans lords besides Him; this rejects claims that Ezra or Christ is God's son and the uncritical adoption of scholars' innovations about lawful and forbidden things.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r3.anchor: يعنى تعالوا إليها حتى لا تقول عزير ابن الله ولا المسيح ابن الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r4.claim: Adi ibn Hatim said they had not worshipped their scholars; Muhammad replied that following their rulings making things lawful and forbidden was worship, and Adi agreed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r4.anchor: وعن عدى بن حاتم ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول

NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r5.claim: If they turn away from monotheism, tell them the proof is established and they must acknowledge that the Muslims are rightly Muslim, like a victor demanding the defeated admit defeat.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p158#3/r5.anchor: أى لزمتكم الحجة فوجب عليكم أن تعترفوا وتسلموا بأنا مسلمون دونكم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and al-Suddī say the address to the People of the Book is directed to the Christians of Najran.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r1.anchor: الخطاب في قول الحسن وابن زيد والسدي لأهل نجران

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r2.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r2.claim: Qatāda, Ibn Jurayj, and others say the address is to the Jews of Medina, who treated their rabbis as lords through obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r2.anchor: وفي قول قتادة وابن جريج وغيرهما ليهود المدينة، خوطبوا بذلك لأنهم جعلوا أحبارهم في الطاعة لهم كالأرباب

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r3.claim: Another view takes the address to include both Jews and Christians.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r4.claim: The Prophet's letter to Heraclius invites him to Islam, promising a doubled reward if he submits and warning him of the burden of his subjects if he turns away; it includes this passage through the command to bear witness that the Muslims submit.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r4.anchor:
وفي كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى هرقل.
" بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من محمد رسول الله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم سلام على من اتبع الهدى أما بعد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r5.claim: Qatāda explains sawāʾ as justice and equity.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r6.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r6.claim: Zuhayr's line uses sawāʾ to convey equal treatment without injustice.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r6.anchor:
وقال زهير:
أروني خطة لا ضيم فيها
يسوي بيننا فيها السواء

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says sawā and suwā can mean justice: with fatḥa the word is lengthened, while kasra or ḍamma shortens it, as in the cited phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r7.anchor: الفراء: ويقال في معنى العدل سوى وسوى، فإذا فتحت السين مددت وإذا كسرت أو ضممت قصرت كقوله تعالى: { مكانا سوى }.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r8.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the phrase as a word of justice between us and you.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r8.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله «إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم»

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r9.speaker: قعنب
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r9.claim: Quʿnubu reads kalima with a still lām, transferring the lām's vowel to the kāf, as in kabid.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r9.anchor: وقرأ قعنب «كلمة» بإسكان اللام، ألقى حركة اللام على الكاف كما يقال كبد.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r10.claim: The invitation is to a just, upright word without deviation from truth, which the verse explains as worshipping God alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r10.anchor: وهو الكلمة العادلة المستقيمة التي ليس فيها ميل عن الحق وقد فسرها بقوله تعالى: { ألا نعبد إلا الله }

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r11.claim: The particle an may be genitive as an appositive to kalima, nominative after an omitted subject, or an explanatory particle with no syntactic position.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r11.anchor: فموضع «أن» خفض على البدل من «كلمة»، أو رفع على إضمار مبتدأ، التقدير هي أن لا نعبد إلا الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r12.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r12.claim: For the explanatory-particle analysis, Sībawayh allows the following verbs to be jussive under lā, or indicative as a predicate or with the sense that we do not worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r12.anchor: هذا مذهب سيبويه. ويجوز على هذا أن ترفع «نعبد» وما بعده يكون خبرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r13.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r13.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ parse the coordinated verbs with jussive mood by analogy, as though the opening an were absent.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r13.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء: { ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ } بالجزم على التوهم أنه ليس في أول الكلام أن.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r14.claim: Not taking one another as lords means not obeying anyone in permitting or prohibiting matters except where God has made them lawful or forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64/r14.anchor: أي لا نتبعه في تحليل شيء أو تحريمه إلا فيما حلله الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r1.claim: This parallels 9:31: people made their rabbis and monks lords by accepting their unauthorized prohibitions and permissions.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.claim: Al-Kiyā al-Ṭabarī says this invalidates bare appeals to juristic preference, such as Abū Ḥanīfa's estimates unsupported by clear evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r2.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: مثل استحسانات أبي حنيفة في التقديرات التي قدرها دون مستندات بينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.claim: The verse also refutes the Rāfiḍīs' claim that an imam's ruling must be accepted without a stated legal basis, including when he declares forbidden things lawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r3.anchor: وفيه رد على الروافض الذين يقولون: يجب قبول قول الإمام دون إبانة مستند شرعي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.claim: Arbāb is the plural of rabb, and dūn here means other than.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r4.anchor: وأرباب جمع رب. و «دون» هنا بمعنى غير.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r5.claim: If they turn away, the Muslims should say they submit to Islam's rules and acknowledge God's blessings, taking neither Jesus, ʿUzayr, angels, nor monks as lords.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r5.anchor: أي أعرضوا عما دعوا إليه. { فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون } أي متصفون بدين الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r6.claim: Jesus, ʿUzayr, and angels are created beings like people, and Muslims must not accept monks' prohibitions of what God has not forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r6.anchor: غير متخذين أحدا ربا لا عيسى ولا عزيرا ولا الملائكة لأنهم بشر مثلنا محدث كحدوثنا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r7.claim: ʿIkrima interprets yatakhidh as prostration; prostration was practiced until the Prophet forbade Muʿādh when he intended to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة: معنى «يتخذ» يسجد. وقد تقدم أن السجود كان إلى زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r8.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet forbade bowing to or embracing one another and instead instructed the Companions to shake hands; Ibn Mājah transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r8.anchor:
وروى أنس بن مالك قال:
" قلنا يا رسول الله، أينحني بعضنا لبعض؟ قال «لا» قلنا: أيعانق بعضنا بعضا؟

QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r9.claim: The author says fuller discussion will follow in Sūrat Yūsuf and Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa, including touching the Qur'an without ritual purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:64#2/r9.anchor: وسيأتي لهذا المعنى زيادة بيان في سورة «يوسف» إن شاء الله، وفي «الواقعة» مس القرآن أو بعضه على غير طهارة

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r1.claim: إلى كلمة attaches to تعالوا, whose object is stated here; an earlier تعالوا focused only on coming, or its destination was omitted as understood to be the mutual imprecation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r1.anchor: فذكر مفعول " تعالوا " بخلاف " تعالوا " قبلها فإنه لم يذكر مفعوله

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r2.claim: The common reading has كلمة with fatḥa on kāf and kasra on lām, its basic form; Abu al-Sammal reads it on the pattern of sidra or ḍarba.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r2.anchor: وقرأ العامة " كلمة " بفتح الكاف وكسر اللام، وهو الأصل. وأبو السمال " كلمة " بزنة سدرة

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r3.claim: كلمة is explained by ألا نعبد, using a part for the whole: the single word denotes a longer statement, as قصيدة may be called قافية.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r3.anchor: من باب إطلاق الجزء، والمراد به الكل، ومنه تسميتهم القصيدة جمعا

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r4.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r4.claim: An anonymous poem uses قافية for the whole poem, not merely one rhyme, illustrating part-for-whole naming.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r4.anchor: وكم علمته نظم القوافي فلما قال قافية هجاني

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r5.claim: The phrase كلمة الشهادة names the whole testimony, and the Prophet’s report about Labid’s most truthful word refers to his line that everything besides God is false.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r5.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r6.claim: Some say the singular كلمة stands for a plural, as in a poem describing many exhausted animals and their bones and hides.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r6.anchor: وقيل: أطلقت الكلمة على الكلمات لارتباط بعضها ببعض

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r7.claim: Another explanation uses singular كلمة for connected words: the tawhid statement functions as one whole because its intended relation fails if a part is missing.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r7.anchor: إذا اختل جزء منها اختلت الكلمة، لأن كلمة التوحيد: لا إله إلا الله

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r8.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r8.claim: The common reading makes سواء genitive as an adjective of كلمة, meaning equitable; Abd Allah’s إلى كلمة عدل explains it but is not a reading.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r8.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " سواء " بالجر نعتا لكلمة بمعنى عدل، ويدل عليه قراءة عبد الله

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r9.claim: سواء is originally a verbal noun; in adjectival use it has three conventional interpretations and remains uninflected in gender, like امرأة عدل.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r9.anchor: و " سواء " في الأصل مصدر، ففي الوصف التأويلات الثلاثة المعروفة

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r10.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r10.claim: Al-Hasan reads سواء in the accusative, either as a verbal noun meaning استوت استواء or as a circumstantial modifier from an indefinite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " سواء " بالنصب وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: نصبها على المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Hawfi take the accusative as a verbal noun, estimating استوت استواء.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r11.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " بمعنى استوت استواء " ، وكذا الحوفي

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r12.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r12.claim: Sibawayh explicitly allows a circumstantial modifier to come from an indefinite noun; the author and al-Shaykh accept that analysis here.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r12.anchor: وقد نص سيبويه عليه واقتاسه، وكذا قال الشيخ

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r13.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r13.claim: Al-Shaykh objects that the verbal-noun reading needs an implied governing verb and an interpretation of سواء as استواء; مستو as an active participle is the more familiar sense.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r13.anchor: والمصدر يحتاج إلى إضمار عامل وإلى تأويل " سواء " بمعنى استواء

SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:3:64/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses سواء as مستوية, supporting the ordinary active-participle sense of equitable.

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r1.claim: ألا نعبد may be a full appositive to كلمة, an appositive to سواء (Abu al-Baqa’s less convincing choice), or an implied subject’s predicate answering what the word is; in these parses it is genitive, and بين is governed by سواء.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه بدل من " كلمة " بدل كل من كل، الثاني: أنه بدل من " سواء "

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa permits ألا نعبد as appositive to سواء, but the author finds this unclear because the described noun, not its adjective, is the main referent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r2.anchor: جوزه أبو البقاء، وليس بواضح، لأن المقصود إنما هو الموصوف لا صفته

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r3.claim: Under the first three parses, بين is an adverb governed by سواء, describing where the equality occurs; Zuhayr’s line is evidence, with a full stop at من دون الله.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r3.anchor: ف " بين " منصوب بسواء ظرف له أي: يقع الاستواء في هذه الجهة

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r4.speaker: زهير
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r4.claim: Zuhayr’s line أرونا خطة لا غيب فيها يسوي بيننا فيها السواء witnesses the construction of سواء with بين.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r4.anchor: أرونا خطة لا غيب فيها يسوي بيننا فيها السواء

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r5.claim: A fourth parse makes أن and its clause a nominative subject, with the preceding adverbial phrase as predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r5.anchor: أن تكون " أن " وما في حيزها في محل رفع بالابتداء، والخبر الظرف قبله

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa also proposes أن نعبد as the subject governed by the preceding adverbial, a parse available only under al-Akhfash and semantically strained.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r6.anchor: جوز أبو البقاء أن يكون فاعلا بالظرف قبله، وهذا إنما يتأتى على رأي الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r7.claim: The fifth parse makes the sentence an adjective of كلمة without a clear linking pronoun; its proposed stop after سواء and restart as a modifier are inconsistent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r7.anchor: وهذا غلط لعدم رابط بين الصفة والموصوف وتقدير العائد ليس بالسهل

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa alternatively says the statement ends at سواء and begins anew with بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد, meaning tawhid between both parties; on this syntax it is a subject-predicate sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r8.anchor: أي بيننا وبينكم التوحيد، فعلى هذا يكون " أن لا نعبد " مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r9.speaker: الزماني
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamani takes ألا نعبد as the subject of سواء, estimating that shared equality between the parties is their not worshipping anyone but God.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r9.anchor: أن يكون " أن لا نعبد " مرفوعا بالفاعلية بسواء، وإلى هذا ذهب الزماني

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r10.claim: Al-Shaykh says al-Zamani’s analysis requires a weak, omitted linking expression فيها.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#2/r10.anchor: إلا أن فيه إضمار الرابط وهو " فيها " وهو ضعيف

SAMIN-DURR:3:64#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#3/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#3/r1.claim: تولوا is past tense; making it present تتولوا would mismatch the addressees, since فقولوا addresses believers while the conditional addresses the polytheists, and would leave the condition without an answer. The implied command is say to them.
SAMIN-DURR:3:64#3/r1.anchor: هو ماض ولا يجوز أن يكون التقدير: " فإن تتولوا " لفساد المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r1.claim: After presenting proofs to Najran's Christians, who declined mutual imprecation and accepted the subordinate status of jizya, the Prophet eager for their faith is directed from polemic to a fair invitation recognized by sound reason and nature.
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r1.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أورد على نصارى نجران أنواع الدلائل وانقطعوا ، ثم دعاهم إلى المباهلة فخافوا وما شرعوا فيها وقبلوا الصغار بأداء الجزية

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r2.claim: The call to an equitable word invites mutual fairness without either side favoring itself, leaving disputation and seeking a fair hearing.
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r2.anchor: هلموا إلى كلمة فيها إنصاف من بعضنا لبعض ، ولا ميل فيه لأحد على صاحبه

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r3.claim: One reported scope of People of the Book is the Christians of Najran.

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r4.claim: A second reported scope is the Jews of Medina.

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r5.claim: A third view says the verse concerns both groups because the wording encompasses them and a reported occasion of revelation names Jews and Christians.
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r5.anchor: أنها نزلت في الفريقين ، ويدل عليه وجهان الأول : أن ظاهر اللفظ يتناولهما

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r6.claim: An occasion report says Jews objected that Muhammad wanted them to treat him as Christians treated Jesus, while Christians said he wanted them to say of him what Jews said about Uzayr.
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r6.anchor: روي في سبب النزول ، أن اليهود قالوا للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام ، ما تريد إلا أن نتخذك ربا كما اتخذت النصارى

RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r7.claim: Razi favors the Christians of Najran because the discourse has just moved from proofs to imprecation and now shifts to fairness; calling them People of the Book honors and soothes them as debate gives way to fair inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v8p75#2/r7.anchor: وعندي أن الأقرب حمله على النصارى ، لما بينا أنه لما أورد الدلائل عليهم أولا ، ثم باهلهم ثانيا

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r1.claim: Ta'ālaw originally meant rising from a low place to a high one, but came to mean turning toward the matter or place to which one is summoned, without physical movement.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r1.anchor: فالمراد تعيين ما دعوا إليه والتوجه إلى النظر فيه وإن لم يكن انتقالا من مكان إلى مكان لأن أصل اللفظ مأخوذ من التعالي

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r2.claim: Sawāʾ means justice and fairness: fairness gives each side half, avoiding wrong to oneself and others, creating equality and balance; taking more than one gives destroys that balance.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r2.anchor: فالمعنى هلموا إلى كلمة فيها إنصاف من بعضنا لبعض ، لا ميل فيه لأحد على صاحبه ، والسواء هو العدل والإنصاف

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses sawāʾ as an adjective of kalima, meaning a word possessing equality: just, upright, and even, so both sides become equal and upright by accepting it.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج { سوآء } نعت للكملة يريد : ذات سواء ، فعلى هذا قوله { كلمة سواء }

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r4.claim: The clause an lā naʿbuda can be nominative through an omitted subject, answering what the word is: it is that we worship only God.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r4.anchor: الأول : إنه رفع بإضمار ، هي : كأن قائلا قال : ما تلك الكلمة ؟ فقيل هي أن لا نعبد إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r5.claim: Alternatively, an lā naʿbuda is genitive as an appositive to kalima.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r5.anchor: والثاني : خفض على البدل من : كلمة

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r6.claim: The three prohibitions answer the Christians' practices: worshipping Christ, associating partners through the three persons they claim are eternal, and treating clergy as lords.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r6.anchor: وإنما ذكر هذه الثلاثة لأن النصارى جمعوا بين هذه الثلاثة فيعبدون غير الله وهو المسيح

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r7.claim: Razi explains that Christians describe three eternal persons as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, with the Word and Holy Spirit hypostases incarnated in Jesus and Mary.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r7.anchor: لأنهم يقولون إنه ثلاثة : أب وابن وروح القدس ، فأثبتوا ذوات ثلاثة قديمة سواء

RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r8.claim: Razi reasons that if the hypostases were not independent they could not separate from the Father's essence and incarnate separately; their independence makes the three-person doctrine shirk.
RAZI-FULL:v8p76/r8.anchor: ولولا كون هذين الأقنومين ذاتين مستقلتين وإلا لما جازت عليهما مفارقة ذات الأب والتدرع بناسوت عيسى ومريم

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r1.claim: One explanation of taking clergy as lords is that Christians obeyed them in declaring things lawful or forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r1.anchor: أحدها : إنهم كانوا يطيعونهم في التحليل والتحريم

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r2.claim: A second explanation is that they prostrated to their clergy.

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r3.claim: Abu Muslim says their ascetics believed divine indwelling appeared in spiritually perfected people, granting powers such as reviving the dead and curing congenital blindness and leprosy; thus they affirmed lordship without using its title.
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : من مذهبهم أن من صار كاملا في الرياضة والمجاهدة يظهر فيه أثر حلول اللاهوت

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r4.claim: A fourth explanation is that they obeyed clergy in sinful acts, which is itself lordship; the Qur'an similarly describes taking desire as a deity (45:23).
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r4.anchor: والرابع : هو أنهم كانوا يطيعون أحبارهم في المعاصي ، ولا معنى للربوبية إلا ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r5.claim: Razi argues these practices are invalid: worship was directed only to God before Jesus and should remain so; shirk is universally false; and obedience in law and conduct belongs to the Creator and Benefactor, not clergy.
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r5.anchor: وكان القول ببطلان هذه الأمور الثلاثة كالأمر المتفق عليه بين جمهور العقلاء وذلك ، لأن قبل المسيح ما كان المعبود إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r6.claim: If they refuse, Muslims should publicly maintain their own submission to God rather than remain preoccupied with forcing others to adopt it.
RAZI-FULL:v8p77/r6.anchor: والمعنى إن أبوا إلا الإصرار ، فقولوا إنا مسلمون ، يعني أظهروا أنكم على هذا الدين

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r1.claim: Sawāʾ can mean just or fair and derives from a root associated with equality, straightness, soundness, proportion, or the middle; sawāʾ al-sabīl idiomatically means the right way.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r1.anchor: a word sometimes understood as meaning “just” or “fair.”

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r2.claim: Some read the call as inviting the People of the Book to a just and fair word, rather than specifically to doctrines shared by Christianity, Judaism, and Islam.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r2.anchor: Thus this phrase is interpreted by some to mean not that the Quran is calling the People of the Book to observe what Christianity or Judaism have in common with Islam, but that this word (or these words) to which the Prophet is calling the People of the Book are just and fair (R).

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r3.speaker: Al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī glosses the shared word as fair treatment by each side toward the other.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r3.anchor: Al-Rāzī glosses it thus: “Come to a word in which there is fair treatment from each of us to the other.”

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r4.claim: Others accept “just” but explain it as common ground because each religion claims to worship God.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r4.anchor: Others, while accepting the gloss of “just,” go on to explain that it refers to what these religions have in common, since they all claim to worship God (M),

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r5.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r5.claim: Others say sawāʾ means what the Quran, Torah, and Gospel do not differ about.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r5.anchor: and others similarly say that sawāʾ refers to that regarding which the Quran, the Torah, and the Gospel do not differ (Z).

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r6.speaker: Ibn Masʿūd
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī cites Ibn Masʿūd’s view that calling someone to a thing’s sawāʾ is calling them to its middle.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r6.anchor: Al-Thaʿlabī quotes an opinion of Ibn Masʿūd that to call some to the sawāʾ of something is to call them to the middle of it.

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r7.claim: Some say the command addresses Jews in and around Madinah; others say it addresses Jews and Christians; some restrict it to Najrān’s Christians.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r7.anchor: For some, the command in this verse was meant to address the Jews in and around Madinah

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r8.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r8.claim: Some explain taking one another as lords as prostrating before people; others mean obeying them against the truth.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r8.anchor: Some understand take one another as lords to mean that one prostrates before them

STUDYQURAN:3:64/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r9.claim: The statement about taking lords apart from God parallels 9:31’s account of rabbis, monks, and the Messiah being taken as lords despite the command to worship one God.
STUDYQURAN:3:64/r9.anchor: This part of the verse is similar to 9:31: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords apart from God

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r1.claim: Al-Tabari explains the invitation to the just shared word as a call to come and approach.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r1.anchor: والإنجيل: {تعالوا} [آل عمران: 61] هلموا {إلى كلمة سواء} [آل عمران: 64] يعني إلى كلمة عدل

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r2.claim: The just word is to worship God alone and renounce every other object of worship or any association with Him.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r2.anchor: والكلمة العدل: هي أن نوحد الله فلا نعبد غيره، ونبرأ من كل معبود سواه فلا نشرك به شيئا

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r3.claim: Taking one another as lords means obeying people when they command disobedience to God and honoring them with prostration as one prostrates to God.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r3.anchor: ولا يدين بعضنا لبعض بالطاعة فيما أمر به من معاصي الله، ويعظمه بالسجود له، كما يسجد لربه

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r4.claim: If the scripture people turn away and do not answer the shared-word invitation, believers should tell them to witness that the believers submit to God.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r4.anchor: فلم يجيبوك إليها، فقولوا أيها المؤمنون للمتولين عن ذلك: اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r5.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet invited the Jews of Medina, who had argued about Abraham, to the just word.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا يهود أهل المدينة إلى الكلمة السواء، وهم الذين حاجوا في إبراهيم»

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r6.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r6.claim: Rabiʿ reports that the Prophet invited the Jews to the shared word.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r6.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: «ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا اليهود إلى كلمة السواء»

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Prophet invited Medina's Jews, who refused, after which he fought them.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: بلغنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا يهود أهل المدينة إلى ذلك، فأبوا عليه، فجاهدهم

TAB-FULL:v5p473/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r8.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar says the verse addressed the Najran delegation, inviting them to a fair proposition that removed their argument.
TAB-FULL:v5p473/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
