TAB-FULL:v5p476/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the Prophet summoned the Christian delegation from Najran to the shared word.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قال: ثم دعاهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعني الوفد من نصارى نجران فقال: {يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd connects the Najran delegation's refusal to accept the invitation with their earlier rejection of the argument about Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r2.anchor: ثنا ابن زيد، قال: قال: يعني جل ثناؤه: " {إن هذا لهو القصص الحق} [آل عمران: 62]

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r3.claim: People of both the Torah and Gospel are addressed: the wording names all scripture people, gives no evidence for singling out one group, and the duty of worshipping God alone applies to everyone commanded.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r3.anchor: لأنهما جميعا من أهل الكتاب، ولم يخصص جل ثناؤه بقوله: {يا أهل الكتاب} [آل عمران: 64] بعضا دون بعض

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r4.claim: تعالوا means come or approach, and is the tafaʿalu form derived from ʿulū, as in expressions meaning draw near.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r4.anchor: وأما تأويل قوله: {تعالوا} [آل عمران: 64] فإنه: أقبلوا وهلموا، وإنما هو «تفاعلوا» من العلو

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r5.claim: Al-Tabari glosses سواء as just or equitable, the meaning of the shared word.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r5.anchor: وقوله: {إلى كلمة سواء} [آل عمران: 64] فإنها الكلمة العدل

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r6.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r6.claim: A Basran grammarian parses سواء in the genitive as an adjective of كلمة meaning just or equal; other nominal and adjectival parses are possible, with the raised adjectival reading preferred, as illustrated at 22:25 and 45:21.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r6.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: جر «سواء» لأنها من صفة الكلمة: وهي العدل، وأراد مستوية

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r7.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r7.claim: A Kufan grammarian treats سواء as a verbal noun used in place of an adjective, with the sense of mutually equal.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r7.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: سواء مصدر وضع موضع الفعل، يعني موضع متساوية ومتساو

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r8.claim: In the sense of justice, سواء also appears as سوى; the Qur'anic phrase مكانا سوى illustrates it.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r8.anchor: وقد يقال في سواء بمعنى عدل: سوى وسوى كما قال جل ثناؤه: {مكانا سوى} [طه: 58]

TAB-FULL:v5p476/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud's recitation has كلمة عدل, a word of justice, in place of كلمة سواء.
TAB-FULL:v5p476/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقرأ ذلك «إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم»

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r1.claim: The address is to the People of the Book, whom al-Ṭabarī identifies here as the people of the Torah.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r1.anchor: قوله: {يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم} [آل عمران: 64]

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r2.claim: Qatāda explains the shared, equitable word as justice between the two sides.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم} [آل عمران: 64] «عدل بيننا وبينكم»

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ gives the same explanation of the shared word as Qatāda.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r3.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا} [آل عمران: 64] بمثله

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the shared word as the declaration that there is no god but God.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r4.anchor: قال أبو العالية: " كلمة السواء: لا إله إلا الله "

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r5.claim: The particle أن is genitive, completing the sense ‘come to [the proposition] that we worship none but God.’
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r5.anchor: فإن «أن» في موضع خفض على معنى: تعالوا إلى أن لا نعبد إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r6.claim: Taking one another as lords means followers obeying leaders in disobedience to God and abandoning obedience to God when leaders forbid it; this is linked to 9:31.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r6.anchor: هو ما كان بطاعة الأتباع الرؤساء فيما أمروهم به من معاصي الله

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says this means not obeying one another in disobedience to God; lordship can also mean obeying chiefs outside ritual worship.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: {ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله} [آل عمران: 64] يقول: " لا يطع بعضنا بعضا في معصية الله

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r8.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r8.claim: ʿIkrima offers bowing or prostrating to one another as another meaning of taking one another as lords.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله} [آل عمران: 64] قال: «سجود بعضهم لبعض»

TAB-FULL:v5p478/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r9.claim: If the invitees turn away and disbelieve, believers should call them to witness that they submit to God alone, inwardly and outwardly.
TAB-FULL:v5p478/r9.anchor: فإن تولى الذين تدعونهم إلى الكلمة السواء عنها وكفروا، فقولوا أنتم أيها المؤمنون لهم: اشهدوا علينا

TABATABAI:3:64/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r1.claim: The passage begins a second phase: after addressing the People of the Book generally, then Christians in particular and believers' alliances, it returns to the People of the Book and later treats related issues.
TABATABAI:3:64/r1.anchor: ثم عادت إلى بيان ما ذكرته ثانيا بلسان آخر ونظم دون النظم السابق فتعرضت لحال أهل الكتاب عامة

TABATABAI:3:64/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r2.claim: The address is to all People of the Book; coming to a word means gathering around its meaning by acting on it, rather than merely reciting a formula.
TABATABAI:3:64/r2.anchor: بالحقيقة إنما هي إلى الاجتماع على معنى الكلمة بالعمل به وإنما تنسب إلى الكلمة لتدل على كونها دائرة بألسنتهم

TABATABAI:3:64/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r3.claim: The invitation means accepting the word together, cooperating to publicize it, and acting on what it requires.
TABATABAI:3:64/r3.anchor: فالمعنى تعالوا نأخذ بهذه الكلمة متعاونين متعاضدين في نشرها والعمل بما توجبه.

TABATABAI:3:64/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r4.claim: Sawa originally means equal at both ends; here it means equal in accepting and acting on the word, so the adjective describes the word through the action related to it.
TABATABAI:3:64/r4.anchor: والسواء في الأصل مصدر ويستعمل وصفا بمعنى مساوي الطرفين وسواء بيننا وبينكم أي مساو من حيث الأخذ والعمل بما توجبه

TABATABAI:3:64/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r5.claim: The wording uses several rhetorical shifts: it attributes gathering to the meaning, substitutes the word for that meaning, then describes the word as equal.
TABATABAI:3:64/r5.anchor: ففي الكلام وجوه من لطائف العنايات نسبة الاجتماع إلى المعنى ثم وضع الكلمة مكان المعنى ثم توصيف الكلمه بالسواء!

TABATABAI:3:64/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:3:64/r6.claim: A reported alternative says the Qur'an, Torah, and Gospel agree on the monotheistic word; the following clause would then state its true meaning against distorted readings and imply rejecting partners.
TABATABAI:3:64/r6.anchor: وربما قيل إن معنى كون الكلمة { سواء } أن القرآن والتوراة والإنجيل متفقة في الدعوة إليها وهي كلمة التوحيد

TABATABAI:3:64/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64/r7.claim: Under that alternative, the clause about not worshiping except God gives the true meaning of the shared word; monotheism entails rejecting partners and lords besides God.
TABATABAI:3:64/r7.anchor: ولازم التوحيد رفض الشركاء وعدم اتخاذ الأرباب من دون الله سبحانه.

TABATABAI:3:64#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r1.claim: The clauses explain the equal word required by submission to God; not worshiping except God means denying worship to any other, rather than proving God's existence.
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r1.anchor: تفسير للكلمة السواء وهي التي يوجبها الإسلام لله. والمراد بقوله { أن لا نعبد إلا الله } ، نفي عبادة غير الله

TABATABAI:3:64#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r2.claim: Because the statement denies partners, its except-God construction is appositional rather than exceptive; the Qur'an treats God's existence and truth as already established.
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r2.anchor: أن لازم كون { إلا الله } بدلا لا استثناء كون الكلام مسوقا لبيان نفي الشريك دون إثبات الإله

TABATABAI:3:64#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r3.claim: The added prohibitions address shirk rooted in beliefs such as divine sonship and trinity: calling worship God-directed does not purify a belief that assigns Him partners.
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r3.anchor: لما كان الكلام مسوقا لنفي الشريك في العبادة ولا ينحسم به مادة الشرك اللازم من اعتقاد البنوة والتثليث ونحو ذلك

TABATABAI:3:64#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r4.claim: Worship directed to one supposed divine partner remains rooted in associating partners, even when that partner alone is named and addressed.
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r4.anchor: والعبادة التي يعبد بها أحد الشريكين وإن خص باسمه ووجه نحوه ليست إلا نابتة منبت التشريك

TABATABAI:3:64#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r5.claim: These three clauses express the purpose of the prophetic mission as it shaped human society.
TABATABAI:3:64#2/r5.anchor: هو الذي يجمع غرض النبوة في السيرة التي كانت الأنبياء تدعو إليها وتبسطها على المجتمع الإنساني.

TABATABAI:3:64-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r1.claim: As explained under 2:213, prophethood is a divine movement to spread religion, whose purpose is to reform human society's course and then the individual's life according to nature and creation.
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r1.anchor: أن النبوة انبعاث إلهي ونهضة حقيقية يراد بها بسط كلمة الدين وأن حقيقة الدين تعديل المجتمع الإنساني في سيره الحيوي

TABATABAI:3:64-78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r2.claim: Prophetic social reform gives society freedom and natural development through justice, and lets individuals pursue life's benefits except where they harm society.
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r2.anchor: موهبة الحرية وسعادة التكامل الفطري على وجه العدل والقسط وكذلك الفرد

TABATABAI:3:64-78/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r3.claim: Freedom and justice remain bounded by servitude to God and submission to the sovereignty of the unseen.
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r3.anchor: وقد قيد جميع ذلك بالعبودية والإسلام لله سبحانه والخضوع لسيطرة الغيب وسلطنته.

TABATABAI:3:64-78/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r4.claim: All prophets call people, individually and collectively, to innate monotheism and to align individual and social conduct with submission to God and justice in rights and good action.
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r4.anchor: يسير النوع الإنساني فرادى ومجتمعين على ما تنطق به فطرتهم من كلمة التوحيد التي تقضي بوجوب تطبيق الأعمال الفردية والاجتماعية على الإسلام لله

TABATABAI:3:64-78/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r5.claim: This order requires uprooting unjust conflict, coercion, enslavement of the weak, and the weak person's subjection to the strong; only God is deity, lord, and judge.
TABATABAI:3:64-78/r5.anchor: ولا يتأتى ذلك إلا بقطع منابت الاختلاف والبغي بغير الحق واستخدام القوى واستعباده للضعيف وتحكمه عليه وتعبد الضعيف للقوي

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r1.speaker: ابن نوح
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r1.claim: Noah says that his people disobeyed him and followed a person whose wealth and children only increased his loss, illustrating prophetic criticism of worldly power.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r1.anchor: رب إنهم عصوني واتبعوا من لم يزده ماله وولده إلا خسارا

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r2.speaker: هود
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r2.claim: Hud condemns his people for building monuments for vanity and factories as if they would live forever.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r2.anchor: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r3.speaker: صالح
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r3.claim: Salih warns his people not to obey those who transgress.

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r4.claim: Abraham challenges his father and people over their devotion to statues and their inherited idolatry.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r4.anchor: ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r5.speaker: موسى
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r5.claim: Moses and Aaron are ordered to go to Pharaoh because he has transgressed and tell him to release the Israelites without tormenting them.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r5.anchor: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r6.speaker: عيسى
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r6.claim: Jesus says he has come to clarify some matters of disagreement, and tells his people to fear God and obey him.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r6.anchor: ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r7.claim: Innate religion rejects oppression, corruption, and illegitimate authorities that destroy happiness and undermine truth.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r7.anchor: فالدين الفطري هو الذي ينفي البغي والفساد وهذه المظالم والسلطات بغير الحق الهادمة لأساس السعادة والمخربة لبنيان الحق والحقيقة

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r8.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r8.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet said that time had returned to its original condition at the creation of the heavens and earth; al-Masudi records this under year ten AH.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r8.anchor: ألا وإن الزمان قد استدار كهيئته يوم خلق الله السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r9.claim: Tabatabai infers that the Prophet meant people were returning to their natural disposition as Islamic practice became established among them.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#2/r9.anchor: وكأنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يريد به رجوع الناس إلى حكم الفطرة باستقرار سيرة الإسلام بينهم.

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r1.claim: God alone is worthy of worship because divinity means that all things seek Him and that He is the source of every perfection needed by creation.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r1.anchor: وهو أن يكون منشأ لكل كمال في الأشياء على كثرتها وارتباطها واتحادها في الحاجة

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r2.claim: Since the universe's beings are bound by one order and their existence is connected, they have one Lord because they have one Creator.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r2.anchor: إذ هؤلاء المربوبون لوحدة نظامهم وارتباط وجودهم لا رب لهم إلا واحد إذ لا خالق لهم إلا واحد.

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r3.claim: Human beings are parts of one human reality and kind, equally endowed by creation; this entails equal rights to life and equal standing.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r3.anchor: أبعاض من حقيقة واحدة هي حقيقة الإنسان ونوعه

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r4.claim: Differences in how people manifest common human gifts assign capacities to those who need them, such as childbirth to women and treatment to the sick, rather than establish superior human rank.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r4.anchor: الولادة يعطاها الإنسان الأنثى والعلاج يعطاه الإنسان المريض.

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r5.claim: One person should not impose will on another; their proper relation is reciprocal cooperation in acquiring life's benefits.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r5.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن يحمل البعض إرادته وهواه على البعض إلا أن يتحمل ما يعادله وهو التعاون على اقتناء مزايا الحياة

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r6.claim: Making one person an absolute ruler over another destroys innate nature and the foundations of humanity.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r6.anchor: ففيه إبطال الفطرة وهدم بنيان الإنسانية.

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r7.claim: Since lordship belongs exclusively to God, a person who lets another control him as an absolute lord has effectively taken a lord besides God.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r7.anchor: الربوبية مما يختص بالله لا رب سواه فتمكين الإنسان مثله من نفسه يتصرف فيه بما يريد

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r8.claim: The prohibition rests on two arguments: human individuals are parts of one kind, and lordship is exclusive to divinity.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r8.anchor: إحداهما كون الأفراد أبعاضا والأخرى كون الربوبية من خصائص الألوهية.

TABATABAI:3:64#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r9.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, the Prophet and his followers declare that they remain on the religion God approves, Islam.
TABATABAI:3:64#3/r9.anchor: استشهاد بأنهم وهم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن اتبعه على الدين المرضي عند الله تعالى وهو الإسلام

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r1.speaker: بعض الروايات
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r1.claim: Some reports say the Prophet invited the Jews of Medina to the common word until they accepted the jizya; Tabatabai says this need not conflict with the verse's descent concerning Najran's delegation.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r1.anchor: وورد في بعض الروايات أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم دعا يهود المدينة إلى الكلمة السواء حتى قبلوا الجزية

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r2.speaker: أبو سفيان
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r2.claim: In a long report from Ibn Abbas, Abu Sufyan recounts the Prophet's letter to Heraclius, which invited him to Islam and quoted this verse; al-Bukhari records it, and Muslim and other compilers also transmit it.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن أبي سفيان في حديث طويل يذكر فيه كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r3.claim: It was also said that the Prophet's letter to Muqawqis included the verse; a Kufi-script manuscript attributed to the Prophet was reproduced and circulated.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r3.anchor: وقد قيل إن كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى مقوقس عظيم القبط أيضا كان مشتملا على قوله

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r4.speaker: المؤرخون
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r4.claim: Historians date the Prophet's letters to the Roman, Persian, and Abyssinian rulers to year six AH, which would put this verse's revelation in year six or earlier.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r4.anchor: كتب الكتب وأرسل الرسل إلى الملوك من قيصر وكسرى والنجاشي سنة ست من الهجرة

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r5.speaker: الطبري وابن الأثير والمقريزي
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r5.claim: These historians date the Christian delegation from Najran to year ten AH, implying that the verse's revelation tied to that visit would be later.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر المؤرخون كالطبري وابن الأثير والمقريزي أن نصارى نجران إنما وفدوا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سنة عشر من الهجرة

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r6.speaker: أبو الفداء وآخرون
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r6.claim: Another historical account dates the Najran delegation to year nine AH, likewise implying a later revelation if the verse descended for that occasion.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r6.anchor: وذكر آخرون كأبي الفداء في البداية والنهاية ونظيره في السيرة الحلبية أن ذلك كان في سنة تسع من الهجرة

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r7.claim: Another view, suggested by later reports, places the verse's revelation at the beginning of the Hijra.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r7.anchor: وربما قيل إن الآية مما نزلت أول الهجرة على ما تشعر به الروايات الآتية

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r8.speaker: ابن حجر
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r8.claim: A further view, transmitted by Ibn Hajar, says the verse was revealed twice.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r8.anchor: وربما قيل إن الآية نزلت مرتين نقله الحافظ ابن حجر.

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r9.claim: The passage's continuity supports revelation before year nine; Tabatabai considers the Najran visit to have occurred in year six or earlier.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r9.anchor: والذي يؤيده اتصال آيات السورة سياقا كما مرت الإشارة إليه في أول السورة أن الآية نزلت قبل سنة تسع

TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r10.claim: It is unlikely that the Prophet would write to the great rulers of Rome, Egypt, and Persia while ignoring nearby Najran, supporting an earlier date for the delegation.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#3/r10.anchor: ومن البعيد أن يكاتب صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عظماء الروم والقبط وفارس ويغمض عن نجران مع قرب الدار.

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r1.speaker: البيهقي
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r1.claim: A report in al-Bayhaqi says the Prophet wrote to Najran before Surah al-Naml was revealed, inviting them to worship God rather than servants and threatening jizya or war if they refused.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r1.anchor: كما عن البيهقي في الدلائل أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه طس سليمان

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r2.claim: Tabatabai finds this chronology untenable because al-Naml is Meccan and its contents clearly predate the Hijra; the reported letter also includes unexplained jizya and war language.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r2.anchor: وذلك أن سورة النمل من السور المكية ومضامين آياتها كالنص في أنها نزلت قبل هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet's letter to the disbelievers included the invitation to a common word.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r3.anchor: أخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس أن كتاب رسول الله إلى الكفار { تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم } الآية.

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Najran's Christians and Jewish scholars disputed whether Abraham was Jewish or Christian, prompting the revelation of the passage about disputing over Abraham.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن إسحاق وابن جرير والبيهقي في الدلائل عن ابن عباس قال اجتمعت نصارى نجران وأحبار يهود عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فتنازعوا عنده

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r5.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r5.claim: In the same report, Abu Rafi and a Najranian ask whether Muhammad wants them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; the Prophet denies this and says God sent him for no such purpose.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r5.anchor: فقال أبو رافع القرظي أتريد منا يا محمد أن نعبدك كما تعبد النصارى عيسى ابن مريم

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r1.claim: Al-Khazin transmits the Abyssinian migration account through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih and Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Ishaq from Ibn Shihab; the report says Quraysh sent Amr and Amara to Najashi after Badr to retrieve the Muslim migrants.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r1.anchor: روى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس ورواه محمد بن إسحاق عن ابن شهاب بإسناده حديث هجرة الحبشة قال لما هاجر جعفر

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r2.speaker: قريش
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r2.claim: After Badr, Quraysh sought revenge for their dead and planned to use gifts to persuade Najashi to hand over the Muslims in Abyssinia.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r2.anchor: اجتمعت قريش في دار الندوة وقالوا إن لنا في الذين عند النجاشي من أصحاب محمد ثأرا ممن قتل منكم ببدر

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r3.speaker: قريش
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r3.claim: Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-As and Amara ibn Abi Muayt with gifts to Abyssinia as their envoys.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r3.anchor: فبعثوا عمرو بن العاص وعمارة بن أبي معيط معهم الهدايا الإدم وغيره

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r4.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r4.claim: Amr portrayed the Muslim migrants as followers of a false prophet who threatened Najashi's religion, rule, and subjects, and urged him to hand them over.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r4.anchor: فقال عمرو بن العاص ألا ترى أنهم يستكبرون أن يسجدوا لك؟

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r5.speaker: جعفر بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r5.claim: Ja'far requests to answer for his companions and tells Najashi that, as a king among the People of the Book, he should hear a fair exchange without injustice.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r5.anchor: قال جعفر أنا قال إنك ملك من ملوك الأرض من أهل الكتاب ولا يصلح عندك كثرة الكلام ولا الظلم

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r6.claim: The Muslims explain that they prostrate only to God, the creator who made Najashi king; their former greeting belonged to their idolatrous past, while the Prophet taught them salam, God's approved greeting and the greeting of Paradise.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r6.anchor: قالوا نسجد لله الذي خلقك وملكك وإنما كانت تلك التحية لنا ونحن نعبد الأوثان فبعث الله فينا نبيا صادقا فأمرنا بالتحية التي رضيها الله وهي السلام تحيه أهل الجنة

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r7.speaker: النجاشي
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r7.claim: Najashi recognizes their account as true and as present in the Torah and Gospel, then asks which visitor called himself a party of God; Ja'far identifies himself.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r7.anchor: فعرف النجاشي أن ذلك حق وأنه في التوراة والإنجيل قال أيكم الهاتف يستأذن عليك حزب الله؟ قال جعفر

TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r8.speaker: النجاشي
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r8.claim: Najashi says that as a king and a person of scripture he will not permit excessive talk or injustice, and asks Amr to speak while the other man listens so he can hear their exchange.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#5/r8.anchor: إنك ملك من ملوك الأرض من أهل الكتاب ولا يصلح عندك كثرة الكلام ولا الظلم وإنما أحب أن أجيب عن أصحابي

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r1.claim: سواء means justice or equity; كلمة can mean a statement explaining a story however long, and Arabs also call an ode a ‘word.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r1.anchor: معنى (سواء) معنى عدل، ومعنى كلمة كلام فيه شرح قصة وإن طال. وكذلك يقول العرب للقصيدة كلمة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r2.claim: The report says Ḥassān ibn Thābit, when asked to recite, asked whether the listener had heard the ‘word of al-Ḥuwaydira,’ meaning his ode beginning بكرت سمية.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r2.anchor: يروى أن حسان بن ثابت الأنصاري كان إذا قيل له أنشد قال للقائل: هل أنشدت كلمة الحويدرة، يعني قصيدته التي أولها:

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r3.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r3.claim: Zuhayr’s verse uses سواء for fairness; linguists gloss it as justice and truth and derive it from the idea of things being equal.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r3.anchor: قال زهير بن أبي سلمى: أروني خطة لا ضيم فيها. . . يسوي بيننا فيها السواء

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r4.claim: One vocalization treats سواء as an adjective of كلمة (‘an equitable word’); another takes it as a verbal noun meaning equality or equivalence.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r4.anchor: فمن قاك سواء جعله نعتا للكلمة يريد ذات سواء، ومن قال سواء جعله مصدرا في معنى استواء

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r5.claim: أن لا نعبد is genitive as an appositive to كلمة; it may instead be nominative as the answer to ‘What is the word?’
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r5.anchor: وموضع (ألا نعبد إلا الله). موضع " أن " خفض على البدل من كلمة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r6.claim: The clause can explain the content of the story, with أن functioning like أي; the chiefs’ ‘walk on’ in 43:23 is a parallel explanatory construction.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r6.anchor: لجاز على أن يكون تفسيرا للقصة في تأويل أي كأنهم قالوا: أي لا نعبد إلا الله - كما قال عز وجل: (وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا)

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r7.claim: A jussive construction is also possible: أن introduces a prohibition, with the speakers as if prohibiting themselves; أن functions as an explanatory equivalent of أي.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r7.anchor: ولوكان (ألا نعبد إلا الله) بالجزم لجاز على أن يكون " أن " كما فسرنا

ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r8.claim: The command not to take one another as lords means returning worship to God and recognizing Jesus as a human like other humans rather than worshipping him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p424/r8.anchor: أي نرجع إلى أن معبودنا الله، وأن عيسى بشر، كما أننا بشر فلا نتخذه

ZAJJAJ:v1p426/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p426/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p426/r1.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, Muslims should testify that they affirm divine oneness and submit to the message brought by earlier prophets.
ZAJJAJ:v1p426/r1.anchor: أي مقرون بالئوحيد مستسلمون لما أتتنا به الأنبياء من قبل الله عز وجل.

TABRISI:3:64/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:3:64/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says kalima means discourse explaining a matter or story, even at length; Ḥassān ibn Thābit called a qaṣīda the “word” of al-Ḥuwaydira and cited its opening line.
TABRISI:3:64/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج معنى كلمة كلام فيه شرح قصة وإن طال ولذلك تقول العرب للقصيدة كلمة

TABRISI:3:64/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r2.claim: Sawāʾ means just or equal; Zuhayr's verses use it for a fair plan without oppression and for equality between parties.
TABRISI:3:64/r2.anchor: ومعنى سواء أي عدل وسوي بمعناه قال زهير: أروني خطة لا ضيم فيها

TABRISI:3:64/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r3.claim: Sawāʾ is also parsed as a verbal noun used for an active participle, meaning a level or equal word.
TABRISI:3:64/r3.anchor: وقيل سواء مستو هو مصدر وضع موضع اسم الفاعل ومعناه إلى كلمة مستوية

TABRISI:3:64/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:3:64/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj regards sawāʾ as a noun rather than an adjective: it is genitive by estimating dhāta, though accusative as a cognate accusative is also allowed.
TABRISI:3:64/r4.anchor: وهو عند الزجاج اسم ليس بصفة وإنما جر بتقدير ذات سواء وجوز نصبه على المصدر

TABRISI:3:64/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r5.claim: An lā naʿbuda may be genitive as an apposition to kalima, meaning “come to the word that we worship none but God.”
TABRISI:3:64/r5.anchor: موضع أن لا نعبد فيه وجهان أحدهما: أن يكون في موضع جر على البدل من كلمة

TABRISI:3:64/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may be nominative under an implied “it is,” introducing the word that follows.
TABRISI:3:64/r6.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون في موضع رفع على تقدير هي أن لا نعبد إلا

TABRISI:3:64/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r7.claim: If read in the nominative, an is lightened from the emphatic particle, approximately “it is that we worship only God”; the final nūn remains in writing, as in the cited verses 20:89 and 21:44.
TABRISI:3:64/r7.anchor: ولو قرئ أن لا نعبد بالرفع كان أن هي المخففة من المثقلة فكأنه قال إنه لا نعبد إلا الله

TABRISI:3:64/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r8.claim: Under the appositional parse, nūn is not written; if read with sukūn, an is explanatory as in “that you should march,” and lā naʿbudu is prohibitive.
TABRISI:3:64/r8.anchor: وعلى الأول يكون من العوامل في الأفعال ولا يثبت في الخط لنون ولو قرئ أن لا نعبد إلا الله بالإسكان فإن مفسرة

TABRISI:3:64/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r9.claim: The author gives three occasion reports: the verse was revealed about Christians of Najrān, according to al-Ḥasan, al-Suddī, Ibn Zayd, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr.
TABRISI:3:64/r9.anchor: أحدها: أنها نزلت في نصارى نجران عن الحسن والسدي وابن زيد ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

TABRISI:3:64/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:3:64/r10.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn Jurayj say it was revealed about the Jews of Medina; the author's companions also transmit this report.
TABRISI:3:64/r10.anchor: وثانيها: أنها نزلت في يهود المدينة عن قتادة والربيع وابن جريج وقد رواه أصحابنا أيضا

TABRISI:3:64/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r11.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:3:64/r11.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī says it concerns both groups of the People of the Book; the author prefers this broader reading because it fits the verse's general wording.
TABRISI:3:64/r11.anchor: وثالثها: أنها نزلت في الفريقين من أهل الكتاب على الظاهر عن أبي علي الجبائي

TABRISI:3:64/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r12.claim: After the argument is complete, God calls the People of the Book to monotheism and to follow the one they acknowledge as having been upon the truth.
TABRISI:3:64/r12.anchor: لما تم الحجاج على القوم دعاهم تعالى إلى التوحيد وإلى الاقتداء بمن اتفقوا أنه كان على الحق

TABRISI:3:64/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r13.claim: The “equal word” is a just, unbiased agreement: worship God alone, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides Him.
TABRISI:3:64/r13.anchor: أي عادلة لا ميل لها كما يقال رجل عدل أي عادل لا ميل فيه

TABRISI:3:64/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r14.claim: One explanation of not taking one another as lords is that they must not make Jesus, one of their own, a lord.
TABRISI:3:64/r14.anchor: ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله } اختلف في معناه فقيل معناه ولا يتخذ بعضنا عيسى ربا

TABRISI:3:64/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64/r15.claim: Another explanation forbids treating the rabbis as lords by obeying them with the obedience owed to lords; the source introduces a supporting verse but the excerpt ends before quoting it.
TABRISI:3:64/r15.anchor: وقيل معناه أن لا نتخذ الأحبار أربابا بأن نطيعهم طاعة الأرباب لقوله:

TABRISI:3:64#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64#2/r1.claim: Tabrisi links the prohibition on taking others as lords to the Qurans charge that Jews and Christians took their scholars and monks as lords.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r1.anchor: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله

TABRISI:3:64#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r2.speaker: أبي عبد الله
TABRISI:3:64#2/r2.claim: They did not worship scholars directly; they treated them as lords by accepting their reversal of what God permits and forbids.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله أنه قال: ما عبدوهم من دون الله ولكن حرموا لهم حلالا

TABRISI:3:64#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r3.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
TABRISI:3:64#2/r3.claim: Adi denied that they worshipped their scholars, and the Prophet answered that obeying their permissions and prohibitions was the relevant worship.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r3.anchor: قال عدي بن حاتم: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله

TABRISI:3:64#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r4.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:3:64#2/r4.claim: The Prophet explains that the people followed religious leaders by accepting what they declared lawful or unlawful.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r4.anchor: أما كانوا يحلون لكم ويحرمون فتأخذون بقولهم

TABRISI:3:64#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64#2/r5.claim: If opponents turn away, Muslims should answer that they are sincere and profess monotheism.

TABRISI:3:64#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64#2/r6.claim: One interpretation takes the Muslims declaration to mean submission to what the Prophet and the prophets brought from God.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r6.anchor: مستسلمون منقادون لما أتى به النبي والأنبياء من الله

TABRISI:3:64#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64#2/r7.claim: A second alternative says the declaration means remaining steadfast in Islam.

TABRISI:3:64#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:64#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:64#2/r8.claim: The instruction trains believers how to answer after an opponent rejects a demonstrated proof: truth remains binding regardless of how many accept it.
TABRISI:3:64#2/r8.anchor: ليعلم المبطل أن مخالفته لا يؤثر في حقه وليدل على أن الحق يجب اتباعه

THALABI:v3p85/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r3.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v3p85/r3.claim: The occasion is a dispute between Najran’s Christians and Jews over whether Abraham was Christian or Jewish; the Prophet rejects both claims, says Abraham was a ḥanīf and that he follows his religion, and calls them to Islam.
THALABI:v3p85/r3.anchor: وقالت اليهود: بل كان يهوديا وأنهم على دينه وأولى الناس به. فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كلا الفريقين بريء من إبراهيم

THALABI:v3p85/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r4.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v3p85/r4.claim: The two groups answer that Muhammad wants them to treat him as a lord, like Christians treat Jesus or Jews treat Ezra, and the verse inviting them to an equal word is revealed.
THALABI:v3p85/r4.anchor: فقالت اليهود: يا محمد ما تريد إلا أن نتخذك ربا كما اتخذت النصارى عيسى ربا.

THALABI:v3p85/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p85/r5.claim: Sawaʾ means justice or equality; Ibn Masʿūd used it for the middle, and the middle is called fair because the fairest and best matters lie in the center, as in ‘the middle of Hell’ (37:55).
THALABI:v3p85/r5.anchor: عدل بيننا وبينكم وكذلك كان يقولها ابن مسعود قال: دعا فلان إلى السواء أي إلى النصف

THALABI:v3p85/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p85/r6.claim: Sawaʾ is a verbal noun used as an adjective for ‘word’; a fatḥa lengthens its vowel, while kasra or ḍamma shortens it, and the Qur’anic ‘an even place’ illustrates the latter form (20:58).
THALABI:v3p85/r6.anchor: وسواء نعت للكلمة إلا أنه مصدر والمصادر لا تثنى ولا تجمع ولا تؤنث.

THALABI:v3p85/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r7.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v3p85/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the clause beginning an lā naʿbuda as nominative, with an implied ‘it is,’ meaning that we worship none but God.
THALABI:v3p85/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: محله رفع [بمعنى أنه لا نعبد]

THALABI:v3p85/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r8.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v3p85/r8.claim: Another grammatical analysis makes the clause accusative by removing a preposition, with the sense ‘that we worship none but God.’
THALABI:v3p85/r8.anchor: وقيل: محله نصب بنزع حرف الصفة معناه: بأن لا نعبد إلا الله.

THALABI:v3p85/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r9.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v3p85/r9.claim: A third analysis makes the clause genitive as an apposition to ‘word,’ meaning ‘come to not worship anyone but God.’
THALABI:v3p85/r9.anchor: وقيل: محله خفض بدلا من الكلمة أي تعالوا أن لا نعبد إلا الله.

THALABI:v3p85/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p85/r10.claim: Not taking one another as lords means rejecting the Jews’ and Christians’ practice of making their scholars and monks lords besides God (9:31).
THALABI:v3p85/r10.anchor: ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله: كما فعلت اليهود والنصارى.

THALABI:v3p85/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p85/r11.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v3p85/r11.claim: ʿIkrima interprets taking one another as lords as their bowing or prostrating to each other.
THALABI:v3p85/r11.anchor: قال عكرمة: هو سجود بعضهم لبعض.

THALABI:v3p86/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p86/r1.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v3p86/r1.claim: Another interpretation says the command forbids obeying anyone in acts of disobedience; a report likens obeying a creature against God to prostrating to someone else.
THALABI:v3p86/r1.anchor: لا تطع في المعاصي أحدا، وفي الخبر من أطاع مخلوقا في معصية الله

THALABI:v3p86/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p86/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p86/r2.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, the Muslims are to tell them to witness that they are sincere in affirming God’s oneness.
THALABI:v3p86/r2.anchor: أنتم لهم اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون: مخلصون بالتوحيد

THALABI:v3p86/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p86/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
THALABI:v3p86/r3.claim: The Prophet’s letter to Heraclius and Rome’s rulers quotes this verse after inviting them to Islam, promising a doubled reward if they accept, and warning that refusal leaves them with the burden of their subjects’ sins.
THALABI:v3p86/r3.anchor: فإني أدعوك إلى الإسلام أسلم تسلم. أسلم يؤتك الله أجرك مرتين.

ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n49/r1.claim: Kalimah literally means word or utterance and is also used philosophically for a proposition or tenet.
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n49/r1.anchor: often used in the philosophical sense of "proposition" or "tenet"

ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r1.claim: Since we refers to human beings, one another also means human beings, so people must not take each other as lords alongside God.
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r1.anchor: the personal pronoun "we" obviously applies to human beings, the expression "one another" necessarily bears the same connotation

ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r2.claim: Asad applies the call to Christians who attribute divinity to Jesus and aspects of it to saints.
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r2.anchor: not merely to the Christians, who attribute divinity to Jesus and certain aspects of divinity to their saints

ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r3.claim: Asad also applies it to Jews who assign quasi-divine authority to Ezra and prominent Talmudic scholars.
ASAD-NOTES:3:64#n50/r3.anchor: but also to the Jews, who assign a quasi-divine authority to Ezra and even to some of their great Talmudic scholars

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r1.speaker: الحسن، والسدي، وابن زيد، ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Suddī, Ibn Zayd, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr identify the addressees as the Christians of Najrān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r1.anchor: الخطاب # لنصارى نجران؛ عند الحسن (¬1)، والسدي (¬2)، وابن زيد (¬3)، ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r2.speaker: قتادة، والربيع، وابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r2.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn Jurayj identify the addressees as the Jews of Medina.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r2.anchor: وليهود المدينة؛ عند قتادة (¬5)، والربيع (¬6)، وابن جريج (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r3.claim: Some commentators say both Jews and Christians are addressed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r4.claim: A kalima may mean an utterance explaining a story, however long; Arabs also call a poem a “word.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r4.anchor: الكلمة: كلام فيه شرح قصة، وإن طال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r5.claim: Sawāʾ means justice; ʿAbd Allāh’s reading has “a word of justice between us and you.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r5.anchor: يريد ب (السواء): العدل، وكذلك في قراءة عبد الله (إلى كلمة عدل بيننا وبينكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses sawāʾ as half or fairness, since the fairest matters are their middle points.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة (¬5): {سواء بيننا وبينكم}؛ أي: نصف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats sawāʾ as an adjective of kalima, meaning a word possessing equality or balance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬2): {سواء}: نعت للكلمة، يريد: ذات سواء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r8.claim: The invitation is to a fair, upright, balanced principle that leaves both sides equal in uprightness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r8.anchor: والمعنى: إلى كلمة عادلة مستقيمة مستوية، إذا أتيناها نحن وأنتم كنا على السواء والاستقامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r9.claim: The clause an lā naʿbuda is genitive as an appositive to kalima and explains that principle: worship none but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r9.anchor: خفض على البدل من {كلمة} المعنى: تعالوا إلى أن لا نعبد إلا الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows the clause to be nominative, as an answer to the question “What is the word?”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p326#3/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): وجائز أن تكون في موضع (رفع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r1.claim: Not associating anything with God means worshipping no other alongside Him; the preposition bāʾ has the sense “with.” An alternative analysis is discussed at 3:151.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r1.anchor: أي: لا نعبد معه غيره. يقال: أشرك معه فلانا: أي: جعله شريكه، وأشرك بالله غيره؛ أي: عبده معه عبادة الله؛ فمعنى الباء، معنى (مع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn ʿAbbās explaining “lords” through Christians taking Jesus and the Children of Israel taking ʿUzayr as lords.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس (¬2): يريد: كما اتخذت النصارى عيسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the parties should worship God and recognize that Jesus is a human like them, not a lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): أي: نرجع إلى أن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r4.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r4.claim: Another explanation is that people must not obey anyone in acts of disobedience; Jews and Christians made their scholars gods by obeying them against God’s command (9:31).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم (¬6): معناه: لا نطيع في المعاصي أحدا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r5.speaker: الخبر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r5.claim: A report says that obeying a created being in disobedience to God is like prostrating to someone other than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p329/r5.anchor: وفي الخبر: (من أطاع مخلوقا في معصية الله، فكأنما # سجد سجدة لغير الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p331/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p331/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p331/r1.claim: If they refuse the invitation, believers should answer their rejection of truth with a contrary declaration that rebukes them: they confess God’s oneness and submit to what the prophets brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p331/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فإن تولوا}. أي: إن أعرضوا عن الإجابة (¬2)، فقابلوا أنتم إعراضهم عن الحق بخلافه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r3.claim: The People of the Book addressed are the Jews of Medina and Christians of Najran; the even word means just speech explaining the account.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r3.anchor: يعني: يهود المدينة، ونصارى نجران { تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء } معنى الكلمة: كلام فيه شرح قصة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r4.claim: The call to worship God alone means worshipping no one alongside Him; taking people as lords refers to Christians treating Jesus and Israelites treating Ezra as lords.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r4.anchor: أي: لا نعبد معه غيره { ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله } كما اتخذت النصارى عيسى، وبنو إسرائيل عزيرا.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r5.claim: Another interpretation forbids obeying anyone in disobedience to God, as in the statement about taking rabbis and monks as lords.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r5.anchor: وقيل: لا نطيع أحدا في معصية الله، كما قال الله في صفتهم لما أطاعوا في معصيته علماءهم:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r6.claim: If they refuse the invitation, Muslims should call them to witness that Muslims submit and affirm God's oneness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:62-64/r6.anchor: أعرضوا عن الإجابة { فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون } مقرون بالتوحيد.

BUKHARI:7/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7/r1.speaker: أبو سفيان
BUKHARI:7/r1.claim: Abu Sufyan reports Heraclius's questions about Muhammad's lineage, reputation, ancestry, followers, apostasy, honesty, wars, and message; Heraclius reads the answers as prophetic signs and predicts Muhammad will rule.
BUKHARI:7/r1.anchor: أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ أَبَا سُفْيَانَ بْنَ حَرْبٍ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ هِرَقْلَ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ

BUKHARI:7/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7/r2.speaker: محمد
BUKHARI:7/r2.claim: Muhammad's letter to Heraclius invites him to Islam and quotes 3:64 as a call to worship Allah alone, renounce shirk and human lordship, and affirm Muslims' identity if the addressees turn away.
BUKHARI:7/r2.anchor: مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ

BUKHARI:7/r3.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7/r3.speaker: أبو سفيان
BUKHARI:7/r3.claim: After the letter is read, Roman notables protest and Abu Sufyan concludes Heraclius fears Muhammad; Abu Sufyan remained convinced Muhammad would prevail until he himself entered Islam.
BUKHARI:7/r3.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَلَمَّا قَالَ مَا قَالَ، وَفَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَةِ الْكِتَابِ كَثُرَ عِنْدَهُ الصَّخَبُ

BUKHARI:7/r4.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7/r4.speaker: ابن الناظور
BUKHARI:7/r4.claim: Ibn al-Natur reports that Heraclius read the stars as foretelling a circumcised king, confirmed the messenger and Arabs were circumcised, received a learned Roman's agreement that a prophet had appeared, then failed to secure Roman allegiance and recast his appeal as a test.
BUKHARI:7/r4.anchor: وَكَانَ ابْنُ النَّاظُورِ صَاحِبُ إِيلِيَاءَ وَهِرَقْلَ سُقُفًّا عَلَى نَصَارَى الشَّأْمِ، يُحَدِّثُ

BUKHARI:2940/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2940/r1.speaker: أبو سفيان
BUKHARI:2940/r1.claim: Abu Sufyan recounts Heraclius's questions about Muhammad's reputation, ancestry, following, apostasy, fidelity, battles, and orders; Heraclius reads the answers as prophetic signs and predicts Muhammad's rule.
BUKHARI:2940/r1.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْلاَ الْحَيَاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ مِنْ أَنْ يَأْثُرَ أَصْحَابِي عَنِّي الْكَذِبَ

BUKHARI:2940/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2940/r2.speaker: محمد
BUKHARI:2940/r2.claim: The Prophet's letter to Caesar urges conversion to Islam, promises a double reward, warns of the subjects' sin if he refuses, and quotes 3:64's call to shared monotheism.
BUKHARI:2940/r2.anchor: مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ، سَلَامٌ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى

BUKHARI:2940/r3.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2940/r3.speaker: أبو سفيان
BUKHARI:2940/r3.claim: After Heraclius reads the letter, Roman dignitaries protest; Abu Sufyan says the king fears Muhammad and he remained certain Muhammad's cause would prevail until entering Islam, though unwillingly.
BUKHARI:2940/r3.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ مَا زِلْتُ ذَلِيلًا مُسْتَيْقِنًا بِأَنَّ أَمْرَهُ سَيَظْهَرُ، حَتَّى أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ قَلْبِي الْإِسْلَامَ وَأَنَا كَارِهٌ

BUKHARI:2941/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2941/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
BUKHARI:2941/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits that the Prophet sent Heraclius a call to Islam; the letter quotes 3:64, inviting the People of the Book to worship God alone, without partners or human lords.
BUKHARI:2941/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أنه أخبره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب إلى قيصر يدعوه إلى الإسلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sawāʾ as justice and cites a poetic line using it for evenness or equal dealing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: عدل. واستشهد بقول الشاعر: تَلاقَيْنا فقاضينا سواءٌ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati says the gloss justice is close because the root's core equality remains in straightness and balance; ʿadl tends toward legal usage, sawiyy toward rectitude, and sawāʾ toward equivalence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r2.anchor: وتفسير سواءٍ بعدل، في آية آل عمران، قريب، ففي العدل دلالةُ المساواة الأصلية في المادة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r3.claim: The word occurs in twenty-six verses chiefly with equality-related contexts; the text also tracks forms of sawā, istawā, and the single sāwā in 18:96.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p394/r3.anchor: وجاءت الكلمة في ست وعشرين آية، سياقها أقربُ إلى معنى المساواة. ومعها من المادة: (الصراط السوىّ)

MUSLIM:4607/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:4607/r1.speaker: أبو سفيان
MUSLIM:4607/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits Abu Sufyan’s account of Heraclius testing Muhammad’s claim and judging the signs prophetic; the Prophet’s letter invites him to Islam and quotes 3:64’s shared call to worship God alone; Abu Sufyan later accepted Islam.

IBNHISHAM:v1p583/r5.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p583/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p583/r5.claim: He calls the People of the Book to a common commitment to worship God alone, associate nothing with Him, and take no one as lord beside Him; if they refuse, Muslims should bear witness to their submission. This invitation cuts off their argument.
IBNHISHAM:v1p583/r5.anchor: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2370/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2370/r1.speaker: أبو سفيان
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2370/r1.claim: Abu Sufyan recounts Heraclius questioning him about Muhammad, then reading the Prophet's letter, which quoted this verse to call the People of the Book to shared monotheism.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2370/r1.anchor: قال أبو سفيان: ثم دعا بكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأمر به، فقرئ فإذا فيه

BURHAN:v1p205/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p205/r1.claim: The Prophet sent six verses to Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib during a dispute with monks and priests; Jaʿfar recited them before the Najāshī, who affirmed their account of Abraham and declared himself an ally of Abraham’s followers, then accepted Islam with his people.
BURHAN:v1p205/r1.anchor: هى ست آيات بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى جعفر بن أبى طالب فى خصومة الرهبان والقسيسين

DAMGHANI:v1p251/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p251/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p251/r6.claim: Sawāʾ means justice; the path and provision examples are likewise glossed as just or equitable.
DAMGHANI:v1p251/r6.anchor: فوجه منها : سواء يعني عدلا قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r1.claim: Kitāb is collected speech in a written document; its root is gathering, as in a gathered military company.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r1.anchor: الكتاب : اسم لكلام مجموع في صك . والأصل فيه : الجمع . ومنه سميت الكتيبة لاجتماعها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba notes that kitāb can name the writer’s act, a verbal noun like qiyām and ṣiyām.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة . ويقال : لفعل الكاتب : كتاب . ويقال : كتب كتابا ، وقام قياما ، وصام صياما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r3.claim: A thing may be named by its maker’s action: a dirham is called the prince’s strike though it is what he struck.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r3.anchor: وقد يسمى الشيء بفعل الفاعل ويقال : هذا درهم ضرب الأمير ، وإنما هو مضروب الأمير

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r12.claim: Kitāb can refer to the Gospel.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p525/r12.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الكتاب في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها :

BURHAN:v1p481/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.claim: Al-ʿIzz cites prophetic supplications and speech, along with the letter to Heraclius and Ibn ʿUmar's wording, as precedents for using Qur'anic language outside recitation and with altered wording.
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.anchor: ورد عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وجهت وجهي والتلاوة

ITQAN:v1p57/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p57/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p57/r10.claim: The text first lists 3:64 and following as material carried to Abyssinia, then says it was carried to the Romans.
ITQAN:v1p57/r10.anchor: ومثال ما حمل إلى الحبشة ﴿ قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء ﴾ الآيات

DAMGHANI:v1p401/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p401/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p401/r3.claim: أهل الكتاب can mean the people of the Gospel.
DAMGHANI:v1p401/r3.anchor: التاسع : الكتاب الإنجيل قوله سبحانه في سورة آل عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p54/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r4.claim: أهل الكتاب can mean readers of the Torah and Gospel.
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r4.anchor: الثاني : الأهل يعني قراء التوراة والإنجيل . قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p408/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r3.claim: The phrase kalimat Allāh or a common word means the testimony that there is no god but God.
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r3.anchor: الكلمة لا إله إلا الله قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says sawāʾ means half or the middle; the middle is fair and balanced.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : [ السواء ] النصف يقال : دعاك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says sawāʾ, sawā, and suwā can mean justice; Zuhayr's poem illustrates equality between parties.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : يقال للعدل سواء وسوى وسوى ، قال زهير بن أبي سلمى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r6.claim: Sawāʾ can mean justice or fairness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p359/r6.anchor: والثاني : العدل . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r5.claim: Ahl al-kitāb means the people who follow the scriptures.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r5.anchor: والثاني : قراء الكتب . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران
